schemaFacts: SCHEMA STATE: user_version = 8, 22 real tables + 1 FTS5 shadow (`exercise_translations_fts`). There is NO workout_* table of any kind yet. The next migration file must be `backend/src/db/migrations/009_*.sql` and must bump to 9. Source of truth for the current shape: `C:/Users/Petike/Documents/Cursor/tracker/docs/brain/20-Data-Model/ERD.md` (generated from the LIVE db by `backend/scripts/brain-gen.mjs`).

THE ROLE ENUM DOES NOT CONTAIN 'client'. `backend/src/db/migrations/001_init.sql:18` is `role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user' CHECK (role IN ('user', 'coach', 'admin'))`. Confirmed by `backend/src/admin/routes.js:164` (`z.enum(['user','coach','admin'])`) and `backend/scripts/seed-dev-users.mjs:20-22`. A 'client' is a `users` row with role='user' that appears as `coach_clients.client_id`. Any new design that says `role='client'` will violate the CHECK.

coach_clients (`006_coaching.sql:23-61`) is THE ownership link: id, coach_id, client_id, team_id NULL, status CHECK IN ('invited','active','archived'), origin CHECK IN ('invite','team_code','pregenerated','manual'), invited_at/accepted_at/archived_at/created_at/updated_at. Indexes: `coach_clients_pair_unique (coach_id, client_id)` UNIQUE (full, not partial — this is what makes `ON CONFLICT(coach_id, client_id) DO UPDATE` legal in `coaching/routes.js:275`), `coach_clients_coach_idx (coach_id, status)`, `coach_clients_client_idx (client_id, status)`, `coach_clients_team_idx (team_id, status)`. A BEFORE INSERT trigger `coach_clients_no_self` RAISE(ABORT)s when coach_id = client_id.

THE ARCHIVE SEMANTICS ARE SPLIT AND INCONSISTENT — pick one deliberately. Archiving sets BOTH `status='archived'` AND `archived_at=unixepoch()` (`coaching/routes.js:137-138`). But the coach's own client list filters `c.status <> 'archived'` (`coaching/routes.js:119`) while the coach's read of a client's onboarding requires `status = 'active'` (`onboarding/routes.js:261`). Reading a plan/log for a client must decide which; `status = 'active'` is the stricter and the one used for cross-user data reads.

exercises (`003_exercises.sql:24-61`, minus name_hu dropped in 005): id, name, normalized_name, description, instructions (JSON array of prose steps), status CHECK IN ('global','private','pending_review','rejected'), owner_id → users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE (NULL = dataset row), rejection_reason, submitted_at, source CHECK IN ('wger','free-exercise-db','custom'), source_uid, difficulty CHECK IN ('beginner','intermediate','advanced'), exercise_type CHECK IN ('strength','stretching','cardio','mobility','plyometrics'), created_at/updated_at/deleted_at. 1652 rows live.

THE EXERCISE VISIBILITY PREDICATE is a single build-time constant at `backend/src/exercises/routes.js:26`: `const VISIBLE = "(e.deleted_at IS NULL AND (e.status = 'global' OR e.owner_id = ?))"`. The `?` is ALWAYS req.user.id. Consequence for plans: a client (role 'user') can only see 'global' exercises plus exercises they own. A coach's own `private` exercise placed into a client's plan is INVISIBLE to that client under this predicate. Any plan/log design must decide how a plan-item grants read access to a non-global exercise, or coaches cannot use their custom library with clients.

onboarding_profiles (`008_onboarding.sql:18-55`) — PK is `user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` (no surrogate id). status CHECK IN ('draft','complete'), step 0..20, primary_goal, experience, sessions_per_week 1..14, session_minutes 10..240, training_location, units CHECK IN ('metric','imperial') — DISPLAY ONLY, everything is STORED METRIC (height_cm REAL, bodyweight_kg REAL). A plan/log schema must store kg and store nothing imperial.

onboarding_equipment (`008:60-64`) is `(user_id, equipment_id) PRIMARY KEY … WITHOUT ROWID`, and its user_id FK points at `onboarding_profiles(user_id)` — NOT at users(id). onboarding_limitations (`008:74-88`) is a rowid table with a surrogate id, `body_area` CHECK over 13 joint-centric codes ('neck','shoulder','elbow','wrist','upper-back','lower-back','hip','knee','ankle','foot','chest','abdomen','other'), `severity` CHECK IN ('past','caution','avoid'), and UNIQUE(user_id, body_area). These two are the ready-made inputs for the 'suggestions filtered by equipment + avoid-list' requirement (T2.5.4 in `docs/brain/00-Index/TODO Phase-2.md` is explicitly blocked only on plans existing).

audit_log (`001_init.sql:69-94`) is APPEND-ONLY, enforced by `audit_log_no_update` / `audit_log_no_delete` BEFORE triggers that `SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'audit_log is append-only')`. Columns: actor_id (→users ON DELETE SET NULL, NULL = system), action TEXT (free-form, no CHECK), target_type TEXT (free-form), target_id INTEGER, detail TEXT (JSON blob), request_id, ip, created_at. Never add an FK INTO audit_log with ON DELETE CASCADE — the delete trigger would abort the parent delete.

There is NO idempotency infrastructure anywhere in the repo — no idempotency_keys table, no request-dedupe column, nothing. Grep for it returns zero hits. The roadmap requirement `T2.10.3` (a replayed set-check must not double-count a PR or a coin reward) has to be designed from scratch.

There is NO coin/reward/gamification table yet, but `T2.10.3` and `docs/brain/00-Index/TODO Phase-7.md:23` ('coin velocity') say rewards are coming and that a replayed log write must not double-award. A log-set design should leave a place for that without inventing the economy.

teams (`006:3-13`): id, coach_id → users ON DELETE CASCADE, name, description, archived_at, created_at, updated_at, index `teams_coach_idx (coach_id, archived_at)`. A team_id sent by a client is validated with an explicit ownership SELECT before use (`coaching/routes.js:168-172`, `310-322`) — that is the existing pattern for a non-row-scoped foreign id.

taxonomy/i18n: muscle_groups(id, slug UNIQUE, name, body_side CHECK IN ('front','back','both'), sort_order) and equipment(id, slug UNIQUE, name, sort_order) after `007_taxonomy_i18n.sql` renamed name_en→name and DROPPED name_hu. Translated labels live in `taxonomy_translations (id, kind CHECK IN ('muscle_group','equipment'), ref_id, lang → languages(code) ON UPDATE CASCADE, name, origin CHECK IN ('manual','dataset','machine'), updated_at, UNIQUE(kind, ref_id, lang))`. `languages` is a WITHOUT ROWID lookup with 23 rows and a partial unique index `languages_single_default ON languages(is_default) WHERE is_default = 1`.

Fallback chain for ANY translated label is written once, in `backend/src/lib/taxonomy.js`: requested lang → instance default (`languages.is_default`) → canonical `name` column on the row, plus a `translated` boolean so the UI can mark a fallback. `labelJoin()` returns a SQL fragment so callers avoid N+1. Any new translated content (e.g. plan/template names shipped by the product) must reuse this shape, not per-language columns.
conventions: PRIMARY KEYS: `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` (rowid alias, never AUTOINCREMENT) on every entity table. One-row-per-user tables use the user id AS the PK instead of a surrogate: `user_theme_prefs.user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` (002:7) and `onboarding_profiles.user_id` (008:20), with the stated reason 'a separate surrogate id would allow two'.

WITHOUT ROWID is used ONLY for: pure composite-key junctions with no extra scalar payload beyond a small enum — `exercise_muscle_map (exercise_id, muscle_group_id)` (003:97-102), `exercise_equipment_map` (003:106-110), `onboarding_equipment (user_id, equipment_id)` (008:60-64) — and small TEXT-keyed lookup tables read whole on every page load: `element_style_config` (002:27-32) and `languages` (004:91-99).

WITHOUT ROWID is deliberately NOT used where an FTS5 external-content index must address the table. `004_translations.sql:12-15` states it verbatim: 'this is a rowid table on purpose, even though (exercise_id, lang) is the natural key. An FTS5 external-content index addresses its source by rowid, and a WITHOUT ROWID table has none — so the composite key lives in a UNIQUE index instead, and a surrogate id carries the FTS link. Getting this wrong fails at CREATE time, which is the good outcome.' Same shape is then copied to `taxonomy_translations` and `onboarding_limitations` (surrogate id + UNIQUE(...)) even without FTS, for uniformity.

TIMESTAMPS: always `INTEGER` unix epoch seconds. In SQL the value is `unixepoch()` (a bare function call, e.g. `created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())`, `SET archived_at = unixepoch()`, `expires_at = unixepoch() + ?`). In JS the comparison form is `Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)` (`coaching/routes.js:257`). No ISO strings anywhere.

SOFT DELETE is a nullable epoch column named `<verb>_at`, filtered with `IS NULL` — never an `is_deleted` boolean. In use: `deleted_at` (exercises, exercise_media), `archived_at` (teams, coach_clients), `revoked_at` (invite_codes), `disabled_at` (users). The delete route is `UPDATE … SET deleted_at = unixepoch() WHERE id = ? AND owner_id = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL` and returns 404 on `changes === 0` (`exercises/routes.js:437-441`).

BOOLEANS are `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (col IN (0, 1))` — see `users.must_change_credentials` (006:111-112), `languages.is_default` / `languages.enabled` (004:96-97). (One legacy exception: `refresh_tokens.revoked` has no CHECK.)

ENUMS are CHECK constraints written inline on the column, all-lowercase bounded codes, never display text: `status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'private' CHECK (status IN ('global','private','pending_review','rejected'))`. Nullable enums are phrased `col TEXT CHECK (col IS NULL OR col IN (…))` (003:45-46) or simply `col TEXT CHECK (col IN (…))` when NULL is allowed by omission of NOT NULL (008:26-29). A LOOKUP TABLE replaces the CHECK only where an admin must edit the set without a migration (muscle_groups, equipment, languages).

Enum code casing is MIXED in the existing schema and there is no single rule: snake_case ('pending_review', 'free-exercise-db' is kebab, 'team_code'), kebab-case ('fat-loss', 'upper-back', 'lower-back', 'smith-machine'). Slugs are kebab ('front-delts'). Pick one and say so; both precedents exist.

OTHER CHECK phrasings in use: GLOB for format (`accent GLOB '#[0-9A-Fa-f]…'` 002:12, `lang GLOB '[a-z][a-z]'` 004:21, `element_id GLOB 'E[0-9]*'` 002:28), BETWEEN for bounded ints/reals (`step BETWEEN 0 AND 20`, `height_cm BETWEEN 90 AND 260`), `length(...)` for text bounds (`length(trim(name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 80` 007:33, `notes IS NULL OR length(notes) <= 2000` 008:50), and plain comparisons (`max_uses > 0`, `uses >= 0`).

INDEX NAMING HAS DRIFTED — both forms are live. Migrations 001–006 use SUFFIX form: `users_email_unique`, `users_role_idx`, `exercises_scope_idx`, `coach_clients_pair_unique`, `exercise_media_exercise_idx`. Migrations 007–008 use PREFIX form: `idx_taxonomy_tr_lookup`, `idx_onboarding_equipment_eq`, `idx_onboarding_limitations_user`. The newest two files use `idx_*`, so that is the trailing convention, but the majority of the schema is `*_idx` / `*_unique`.

INDEXES ARE JUSTIFIED IN A COMMENT ABOVE THEM, naming the query they serve — e.g. 006:43 '-- The dashboard's main query: my clients, by status.' Composite column order follows the actual filter order: `exercises (status, owner_id, deleted_at)` because 'EVERY list query filters on visibility before anything else' (003:54). Ownership indexes are always composite with the discriminating column: `(owner_id, deleted_at)`, `(coach_id, status)`, `(client_id, status)`.

PARTIAL UNIQUE INDEXES are the tool for conditional uniqueness: `exercises_source_uid_unique ON exercises (source, source_uid) WHERE source_uid IS NOT NULL` (003:60-61) and `languages_single_default ON languages (is_default) WHERE is_default = 1` (004:105). Expression indexes are used too: `users_email_unique ON users (lower(trim(email)))` (001:31).

TRIGGERS — two forms in use. 001–006 form (majority): `CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS <table>_updated_at AFTER UPDATE ON <table> FOR EACH ROW BEGIN UPDATE <table> SET updated_at = unixepoch() WHERE id = OLD.id; END;`. 008 form (newest, safer): `CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_onboarding_touch AFTER UPDATE ON onboarding_profiles FOR EACH ROW WHEN NEW.updated_at = OLD.updated_at BEGIN UPDATE … END;` — the WHEN guard is documented as 'so that the trigger cannot recurse through its own UPDATE'.

CONSTRAINT-ENFORCING TRIGGERS are `BEFORE <op> ON <table> [WHEN cond] BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'human message'); END;` — see `audit_log_no_update` / `audit_log_no_delete` (001:84-94) and `coach_clients_no_self` (006:56-61).

FTS5 triggers are a fixed three-trigger set (`<t>_fts_insert` / `_fts_delete` / `_fts_update`) with the delete/update pair emitting the `INSERT INTO <fts>(<fts>, rowid, …) VALUES ('delete', old.…)` incantation, plus an explicit backfill `INSERT INTO <fts> (rowid, …) SELECT …` because an external-content table starts empty (004:65-87).

FOREIGN KEY ACTIONS: owned/dependent rows use `ON DELETE CASCADE`; actor / soft-reference columns use `ON DELETE SET NULL` (audit_log.actor_id, users.created_by, coach_clients.team_id, invite_redemptions.code_id/user_id, referrals.code_id). `ON UPDATE CASCADE` appears exactly once, on `taxonomy_translations.lang → languages(code)`.

MIGRATION FILES: `NNN_name.sql`, the number IS the target user_version (`db/index.js:39-46` validates `/^\d+_.*\.sql$/` and takes the number from the filename). Every file opens with a `-- NNN_name.sql — one-line purpose` header followed by a prose rationale block explaining WHY the shape was chosen, and every non-obvious column carries its own comment. All DDL is `CREATE TABLE/INDEX/TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS`. Seed data is `INSERT OR IGNORE`. Backfills are `INSERT OR IGNORE … SELECT …` from the table being replaced.

DECOMMISSIONING a superseded column/table is a SEPARATE numbered migration that drops it, with the reason stated ('dead schema is not harmless') — `005_drop_legacy_text.sql`. Triggers naming a column must be DROPped before `ALTER TABLE … DROP COLUMN` (005:11).

ORDERING COLUMNS: taxonomy tables use `sort_order INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`; `exercise_media` uses `position INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` and indexes `(exercise_id, deleted_at, position)`. Both names exist; `order` is a SQL keyword and is used nowhere.

JSON columns are allowed ONLY for non-relational blobs and are commented as such: `exercises.instructions` ('JSON array of steps: ordered prose, not a relation'), `user_theme_prefs.gradient`, `audit_log.detail` ('JSON blob: non-relational context only, never a relation'). ERD.md:80 restates the rule.
constraints: THE ENTIRE PUBLIC API IS FIVE FUNCTIONS, in `backend/src/db/index.js:24-28`: `all(sql, params=[]) -> Promise<row[]>`, `get(sql, params=[]) -> Promise<row|undefined>`, `run(sql, params=[]) -> Promise<{changes, lastInsertRowid}>`, `writeTx(steps) -> Promise<{changes,lastInsertRowid}[]>`, `closePool()`. Plus `migrate()` and `ping()`. Nothing outside `src/db/` may import better-sqlite3 (stated at `index.js:2-3`).

`writeTx(steps)` takes ONLY an array of `{ sql, params }` and returns an array of `{changes, lastInsertRowid}` in step order (`worker.js:100-114`). It runs `tx.immediate(steps)` — one IMMEDIATE transaction, write lock taken up front. Callers destructure positionally: `const [consumed, linked] = await db.writeTx([...])` (`coaching/routes.js:297`), `const [updated] = await db.writeTx([...])` (`admin/routes.js:135`).

writeTx CANNOT branch, CANNOT read, CANNOT inspect an intermediate result, CANNOT compute anything. `worker.js:97-99` states it: 'writeTx is for SIMPLE multi-statement writes only. Anything with a guard or a branch — money, inventory, anything irreversible — gets its own NAMED worker function, because writeTx cannot inspect an intermediate result and therefore cannot enforce a condition.' PR detection, 1RM comparison, idempotency lookup, and volume rollups therefore CANNOT be done with writeTx.

ADDING A NAMED WORKER TRANSACTION is a two-file change and there is currently no example of one in the live code (only `migrate` uses the mechanism): (1) `export function myTx({...args})` in `backend/src/db/worker.js`, doing `getDb().transaction(...)` and `.immediate(...)`; (2) a facade line in `backend/src/db/index.js`: `export const myTx = (args) => pool.run(args, { name: 'myTx' });`. Piscina's `{ name }` option selects the named export. Arguments and return values cross a structured-clone boundary, so they must be plain JSON-able data — no Date, no BigInt, no class instances, no functions.

BETTER-SQLITE3 TRANSACTIONS COMMIT ON RETURN — ONLY `throw` ROLLS BACK. This is codified as law in `docs/brain/60-Decisions/0005 Worker tx commit-on-return law.md`: 'ALL validation that can produce an error result runs BEFORE the first write statement. After any write, the tx body may only complete — never conditionally return an error result. If post-write failure semantics are ever needed, throw a typed error and let the route map it.' A `return { code: 'VALIDATION' }` after a write silently commits the write while the client sees a 400.

ERRORS surface as a plain `Error` with `.code` = the SQLite code and a message of the form `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_CHECK: <message> — while running: <first 200 chars of SQL>` (`worker.js:61-67`). This wrapper exists because structured clone strips better-sqlite3's non-enumerable error fields. There is NO typed error mapping: a raised CHECK/FK/UNIQUE violation reaching the route becomes a generic 500 via `errorHandler` (`lib/http.js:62-63`). Constraints must therefore be treated as backstops, with zod + explicit SELECT checks producing the user-facing 400 — exactly the reasoning at `onboarding/routes.js:169-173`.

EVERY `db.all/get/run` CALL IS A SEPARATE POOL TASK AND MAY LAND ON A DIFFERENT WORKER, i.e. a DIFFERENT connection (`worker.js:12-41`, one `db` per thread). Consequences: no session state, no temp tables, no `PRAGMA` side effects, and `last_insert_rowid()` is meaningful ONLY inside a single `writeTx` call. Sequential `await`s are safe (WAL commits are immediately visible to other connections); `Promise.all` fans out to genuinely concurrent connections.

`db.run` and `db.get` are AUTOCOMMIT — each is its own transaction. In `coaching/routes.js:290-293` the referral insert and the redemption records are separate commits from the join writeTx, on purpose. A design that needs 'these three writes are atomic' must put all three into ONE writeTx or ONE named tx.

PRAGMAS SET PER CONNECTION (`worker.js:24-32`, in this exact order): `hexkey` (scrypt-derived), `busy_timeout = 5000` (set BEFORE the WAL switch, deliberately), a `SELECT 1` probe, `journal_mode = WAL`, `synchronous = NORMAL`, `foreign_keys = ON`. NOT set: `recursive_triggers` (so it is OFF — the 001-style self-UPDATE triggers do not recurse today), `defensive`, `cell_size_check`, `case_sensitive_like`.

MIGRATIONS run as ONE `pool.run({files}, {name:'migrate'})` at boot from `server.js:31`, before the port is bound. Inside, each file is `conn.exec(sql)` + `conn.pragma('user_version = N')` in ONE `tx.immediate()` (`worker.js:124-142`). Therefore a migration file MUST NOT contain `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`, and MUST NOT rely on `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` (a no-op inside a transaction) — which means the standard 12-step 'rebuild the table to change a constraint' procedure is NOT available. Only `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` / `RENAME COLUMN` / `DROP COLUMN` and fresh CREATEs are.

`ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` in SQLite forbids a non-constant DEFAULT. You CANNOT add `created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())` to an existing table. This is why 006 could only add `must_change_credentials INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` and a nullable `created_by`. A new column on an existing table must be nullable or have a literal constant default.

The prepared-statement cache is `const statements = new Map()` keyed on the EXACT SQL string, per worker, NEVER evicted (`worker.js:43-51`). Dynamically assembled SQL creates one cache entry per distinct shape. Existing code does this deliberately and boundedly: `IN (${wanted.map(() => '?').join(',')})` built from the array's LENGTH, contents always bound (`onboarding/routes.js:175-178`, comment at 173-174). An unbounded number of shapes is a slow memory leak.

`lastInsertRowid` is returned from `sqlite3_last_insert_rowid()` and is NOT updated by inserts into WITHOUT ROWID tables. Inserting into `onboarding_equipment` / `exercise_muscle_map` returns a stale value from an unrelated earlier insert on that connection. Only trust it after an insert into a rowid table.

Pool sizing: `minThreads = maxThreads = env.DB_POOL_THREADS ?? Math.max(2, availableParallelism() - 1)` and pinned so workers are never torn down — each respawn costs a ~200ms scrypt KDF plus a reopen (`index.js:13-22`). A long-running write transaction holds the single SQLite write lock; other writers wait up to `busy_timeout = 5000` then get SQLITE_BUSY. Keep named transactions short.

ROUTE-LAYER CONTRACT every new endpoint must follow (seen in all five routers): `asyncRoute(async (req, res) => …)`, zod `.strict()` schema parsed FIRST, `z.coerce.number().int().positive().parse(req.params.id)` for path ids, `rateLimit({ windowMs: 15*60*1000, limit: N, standardHeaders: true, legacyHeaders: false, skip: () => process.env.NODE_ENV === 'test' })` per tier (read 600, write 60, admin 120, autosave 240, redeem 10), errors only via `sendError(res, status, ERR.<CODE>, 'prose')` from `lib/http.js`. Cursor pagination via `encodeCursor/decodeCursor/clampLimit` (`lib/cursor.js`, MAX_PAGE = 24). Sort keys from a constant map, never a query-string column name (`exercises/routes.js:29-32`).

There is NO test suite — `backend/tests/` does not exist. The only automated coverage is `backend/scripts/smoke.js` (+ `smoke-run.mjs`, `smoke-limits.js`), and `docs/brain/00-Index/TODO Phase-2.md` gate T2.11.2 says every new endpoint must be added to it.
surprises: THE BRIEF'S SCHEMA SUMMARY IS WRONG ABOUT THE ROLE ENUM. There is no `'client'` role — it is `CHECK (role IN ('user', 'coach', 'admin'))` (001:18). Designing plan/log tables around `role='client'` produces a schema that cannot be written to.

404-NOT-403 APPLIES TO ROW OWNERSHIP ONLY. Role gates DO return 403: `requireCoach` (`coaching/routes.js:60-63`), `requireRole` (`auth/middleware.js:119-122`), the coach/admin check in `exercises/routes.js:318-320`, and the pre-generated-account gate (`middleware.js:92`). The 404 rule is for 'this id is not yours or does not exist' — `exercises/routes.js:22-25` explains why: 'A 403 confirms the id is real, and that is enough to enumerate another coach's private library.'

THE OWNERSHIP PROOF IS THE LINK ID, NOT THE CLIENT'S USER ID. `onboarding/routes.js:255-265` is the canonical cross-user read, verbatim: `const link = await db.get(\`SELECT client_id FROM coach_clients WHERE id = ? AND coach_id = ? AND status = 'active'\`, [linkId, req.user.id]); if (!link) return sendError(res, 404, ERR.NOT_FOUND, 'not found');` — with the comment 'An archived link matches nothing, so access ends the moment it is archived rather than at the next token refresh.' A plan/log API keyed on `/clients/:userId/...` would break this property; key it on the LINK id.

THE 001-STYLE `updated_at` TRIGGER SILENTLY CLOBBERS ANY updated_at YOU SET YOURSELF. `AFTER UPDATE ON t BEGIN UPDATE t SET updated_at = unixepoch() WHERE id = OLD.id; END;` has no WHEN guard, so it rewrites the column after every update. It is only non-recursive because `PRAGMA recursive_triggers` is left at its default OFF — which `worker.js` never sets explicitly. Turning it on would infinite-loop six tables. The 008 form (`WHEN NEW.updated_at = OLD.updated_at`) is immune and is the newest precedent.

WITHOUT ROWID + FTS5 IS A HARD INCOMPATIBILITY, and it is the single most explicitly documented trap in the repo (`004_translations.sql:12-15`). If any new table (e.g. a plan/template name that should be searchable) needs FTS5 external content, it MUST be a rowid table with a surrogate `id` and a UNIQUE index on the natural key. If it does not need FTS, a composite-PK WITHOUT ROWID junction is the convention.

THE WHOLE APP HAS EXACTLY ZERO NAMED WORKER TRANSACTIONS. Every write today goes through the generic `writeTx`, whose steps cannot branch. The Phase-2 execution features — PR detection, Epley 1RM, idempotent set-check — are the FIRST features that structurally require the named-worker-function mechanism. That mechanism exists (Piscina `{name}`) but is unexercised outside `migrate`, so the design must specify both halves (worker export + index.js facade) or it is not implementable.

ADR-0005 IS MARKED HISTORICAL BUT ITS LESSON IS STILL BINDING. `docs/brain/60-Decisions/0005 Worker tx commit-on-return law.md` carries a banner saying the code it described was deleted in the 2026-08-04 full rebuild (ADR-0006). The commit-on-return behaviour of better-sqlite3 is a library property, not a code property — it still applies to every named transaction you write. Do not dismiss the file because it says HISTORICAL.

THE COACH'S PRIVATE EXERCISES ARE INVISIBLE TO THEIR CLIENTS under the existing VISIBLE predicate (`exercises/routes.js:26`). Nothing in the schema currently grants a client read access to a non-global exercise, and `coach_clients` is not consulted anywhere in `exercises/routes.js`. Any plan design must confront this explicitly — either by extending VISIBLE with a coach_clients EXISTS clause, or by snapshotting exercise identity into the plan item. Silence on this point produces a plan whose exercises 404 for the client.

COMPLETE-STATE IS SERVER-DECIDED AND NOT CLIENT-WRITABLE, via an explicit column allow-list. `onboarding/routes.js:83-91`: `WRITABLE` lists the twelve columns a PATCH may touch and `status`/`completed_at` are deliberately absent, with the comment 'Spreading the request body into an UPDATE is how `status` or `completed_at` ends up client-controlled.' The same shape appears in `exercises/routes.js:408-419` (`put(col, value)` pick-list). Copy this, do not spread req.body.

SET-REPLACEMENT IS DELETE-THEN-INSERT INSIDE ONE writeTx, NOT A DELTA API — `onboarding/routes.js:189-199`: 'Replace-in-place: delete then insert, inside the same transaction, so the set is never momentarily empty for a concurrent reader.' Duplicates in the incoming array are de-duped in JS before the inserts because 'UNIQUE would abort the whole save over a UI dupe' (line 206). This is the precedent for plan-day/item reordering payloads.

'ALREADY DONE' IS NOT AN ERROR when the action is idempotent-by-nature: `onboarding/routes.js:237-244` returns `{ ok: true, alreadyComplete: result.changes === 0 }` because 'a double-tapped submit button is the client's most ordinary mistake and must not read as a failure'. But the same `changes === 0` is a 404 for ownership misses and a 409 for exhausted/already-decided (`admin/routes.js:157`, `coaching/routes.js:286`). The mapping of `changes === 0` to a status code is a per-endpoint decision, not a rule.

MIGRATION IDEMPOTENCY IS ONLY VIA user_version FOR `ALTER TABLE`. Every CREATE uses `IF NOT EXISTS`, but `ALTER TABLE` has no such clause (006:111-113, 007:23-24, 007:67-68, 005:18). A migration file is therefore NOT re-runnable on its own — it is safe only because `worker.js:131` skips it when `version <= user_version`. Never hand-run a migration file.

`brain-gen.mjs` EXCLUDES ANY TABLE WHOSE NAME MATCHES `%_fts%` from the generated docs (`backend/scripts/brain-gen.mjs:28`). Naming a real table something containing `_fts` would make it silently vanish from `docs/brain/20-Data-Model/`. Also: after any migration, `npm run brain:gen` must be run — `ERD.md` and the per-table pages are generated from the LIVE database, not from the .sql files, and gate T2.11.7 requires it.

UNITS ARE A DISPLAY PREFERENCE, NOT A STORAGE FORMAT (008:38-39): 'Everything is STORED metric so that no conversion can ever happen twice, and the imperial user sees a converted view of a single canonical number.' A `workout_log_sets.weight` column must be kg, full stop — and the client's `units` value must never reach a write path as a discriminator.

THE EXISTING JOIN-CODE FLOW IS THE ONLY LIVE EXAMPLE OF A GUARD-IN-UPDATE INSIDE A TRANSACTION, and it is worth copying verbatim (`coaching/routes.js:267-287`): step 1 is `UPDATE invite_codes SET uses = uses + 1 WHERE id = ? AND uses < max_uses AND revoked_at IS NULL`, step 2 is the upsert, and the route checks `consumed.changes === 0` AFTER the transaction has committed to decide the response. That works because both steps are harmless when the guard fails — the pattern does NOT generalise to a case where step 2 must not happen when step 1 fails. For that you need a named transaction that throws.

`app.use('/api/v1', mediaRoutes)` is mounted BEFORE `app.use(csrfProtection)` in `backend/server.js:146-148`, so the media router is outside CSRF protection (multipart uploads cannot be JSON). Any new router added after line 148 gets CSRF for free; anything added before it does not. Mount plan/log routers after line 148.

designs.name: 009_workouts — "Snapshot Session": an execution-first plan & log schema
designs.thesis: The workout session is a self-contained snapshot minted at start — every set row, its prescription, and the pointer to last time's performance are materialised in one write — so that the player needs zero network and zero joins to the plan while the client is training, the log can never change retroactively when the plan is edited, and a freestyle session is the same object with two NULLs.

tables.name: workout_plans
tables.purpose: The authoring root. One row is either a template (client_id NULL, is_template 1), a coach's unassigned draft, or a plan assigned to one client. `version` is bumped on every structural edit and snapshotted onto each log, so a session can always say which shape of the plan produced it. Soft-deleted, never hard-deleted, so a log's provenance breadcrumb survives.
tables.ddl:
-- The authoring root. `owner_id` is whoever wrote it (coach, or the client for a self-made
-- plan); NULL is reserved for product-shipped stock templates, exactly as `exercises.owner_id
-- IS NULL` means a dataset row. `client_id` is the assignment; a template is never assigned.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_plans (
  id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  owner_id       INTEGER REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  client_id      INTEGER REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  is_template    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (is_template IN (0, 1)),
  -- Provenance of a clone-to-client. SET NULL: deleting the template must not delete the
  -- plans a client is actually training on.
  source_plan_id INTEGER REFERENCES workout_plans(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,

  title       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(title)) BETWEEN 1 AND 120),
  -- Which language the coach WROTE this in. Coach prose is never machine-translated (same
  -- reasoning as onboarding_profiles.notes); this only lets the UI mark it honestly.
  title_lang  TEXT CHECK (title_lang IS NULL OR title_lang GLOB '[a-z][a-z]'),
  description TEXT CHECK (description IS NULL OR length(description) <= 2000),
  goal        TEXT CHECK (goal IS NULL OR goal IN (
                'strength', 'muscle', 'fat-loss', 'endurance', 'mobility', 'health', 'sport')),

  -- A CIVIL DATE, not an epoch. A workout scheduled for Tuesday must stay on Tuesday when the
  -- client flies to another timezone; an epoch instant would silently slide a day. The epoch
  -- rule governs instants, and a scheduled day is not an instant.
  start_date TEXT CHECK (start_date IS NULL OR start_date GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]'),
  -- IANA name, needed to emit correct ICS and to resolve "today" for the home card.
  timezone   TEXT CHECK (timezone IS NULL OR length(timezone) BETWEEN 3 AND 64),
  week_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (week_count BETWEEN 1 AND 52),
  -- When 1 the block cycles forever, so the calendar and the home card always find a day.
  repeats    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (repeats IN (0, 1)),

  status  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'active', 'paused', 'completed')),
  -- Bumped by every structural edit. Snapshotted onto workout_logs.plan_version so a log can
  -- say "the plan has changed since you did this" without keeping a copy of the plan.
  version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (version > 0),

  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  deleted_at INTEGER,

  -- A template belongs to a library, not to a person.
  CHECK (is_template = 0 OR client_id IS NULL),
  -- Only a stock template may be ownerless.
  CHECK (owner_id IS NOT NULL OR is_template = 1)
);

-- The client's own plan list and the home card's "which plan is live for me".
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_plans_client ON workout_plans (client_id, status, deleted_at);
-- The coach's library and the template picker.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_plans_owner  ON workout_plans (owner_id, is_template, deleted_at);
-- "which plans came from this template", for the clone-provenance panel.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_plans_source ON workout_plans (source_plan_id);

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_workout_plans_touch
AFTER UPDATE ON workout_plans FOR EACH ROW
WHEN NEW.updated_at = OLD.updated_at
BEGIN
  UPDATE workout_plans SET updated_at = unixepoch() WHERE id = NEW.id;
END;

tables.name: workout_plan_days
tables.purpose: One day of a plan, addressed by (week_index, weekday) for calendar-anchored plans or by (week_index, position) for free-floating ones. A rest day is a real row, because the calendar and the adherence ring both need to know a rest day was prescribed rather than missed.
tables.ddl:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_plan_days (
  id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  plan_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_plan_days_parent_guard_placeholder_removed_plan(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  week_index INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (week_index BETWEEN 0 AND 51),
  -- 0 = Monday. NULL for a plan that is a sequence rather than a calendar ("day 1, day 2").
  weekday    INTEGER CHECK (weekday IS NULL OR weekday BETWEEN 0 AND 6),
  position   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (position >= 0),
  title      TEXT CHECK (title IS NULL OR length(trim(title)) BETWEEN 1 AND 80),
  notes      TEXT CHECK (notes IS NULL OR length(notes) <= 2000),
  -- A prescribed rest day is data, not the absence of data: adherence must not count it as missed.
  is_rest    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (is_rest IN (0, 1)),
  est_minutes INTEGER CHECK (est_minutes IS NULL OR est_minutes BETWEEN 5 AND 300),
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())
);

-- The week view reads a whole plan in slot order; copy-week reads one week.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_plan_days_plan ON workout_plan_days (plan_id, week_index, position);
-- Two workouts cannot occupy the same calendar slot; free-floating days (weekday NULL) are exempt.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_plan_days_slot
  ON workout_plan_days (plan_id, week_index, weekday) WHERE weekday IS NOT NULL;

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_workout_plan_days_touch
AFTER UPDATE ON workout_plan_days FOR EACH ROW
WHEN NEW.updated_at = OLD.updated_at
BEGIN
  UPDATE workout_plan_days SET updated_at = unixepoch() WHERE id = NEW.id;
END;

tables.name: workout_plan_items
tables.purpose: One prescribed exercise inside a day. Carries the flat prescription (the common case), the superset/circuit grouping, and the rest interval. `prescription_kind` is the discriminator that tells the player whether to render reps, a clock, or a distance — and a table CHECK makes an inconsistent prescription unwritable.
tables.ddl:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_plan_items (
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  day_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_plan_days(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- CASCADE here, SET NULL on the LOG side. A vanished exercise should drop out of a live plan;
  -- it must never rewrite history.
  exercise_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES exercises(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  position    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (position >= 0),

  -- Items sharing (day_id, group_index) are performed together. An INTEGER rather than a label
  -- so the grouping also orders; NULL means a standalone exercise.
  group_index INTEGER CHECK (group_index IS NULL OR group_index BETWEEN 0 AND 50),
  group_kind  TEXT CHECK (group_kind IS NULL OR group_kind IN ('superset', 'circuit')),

  prescription_kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'reps' CHECK (prescription_kind IN ('reps', 'time', 'distance')),
  target_sets       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 3 CHECK (target_sets BETWEEN 1 AND 20),
  target_reps_min   INTEGER CHECK (target_reps_min IS NULL OR target_reps_min BETWEEN 1 AND 200),
  target_reps_max   INTEGER CHECK (target_reps_max IS NULL OR target_reps_max BETWEEN 1 AND 200),
  -- kg, always. `onboarding_profiles.units` is a display preference and must never reach a write.
  target_weight_kg  REAL CHECK (target_weight_kg IS NULL OR (target_weight_kg >= 0 AND target_weight_kg <= 1000)),
  target_percent_1rm INTEGER CHECK (target_percent_1rm IS NULL OR target_percent_1rm BETWEEN 10 AND 150),
  target_duration_seconds INTEGER CHECK (target_duration_seconds IS NULL OR target_duration_seconds BETWEEN 1 AND 36000),
  target_distance_m INTEGER CHECK (target_distance_m IS NULL OR target_distance_m BETWEEN 1 AND 200000),
  target_rpe        REAL CHECK (target_rpe IS NULL OR (target_rpe >= 1 AND target_rpe <= 10)),
  rest_seconds      INTEGER CHECK (rest_seconds IS NULL OR rest_seconds BETWEEN 0 AND 3600),
  -- Eccentric/pause/concentric/pause, 'X' for explosive.
  tempo             TEXT CHECK (tempo IS NULL OR tempo GLOB '[0-9X][0-9X][0-9X][0-9X]'),
  notes             TEXT CHECK (notes IS NULL OR length(notes) <= 1000),

  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),

  CHECK (target_reps_max IS NULL OR target_reps_min IS NULL OR target_reps_max >= target_reps_min),
  -- A grouping without a kind renders as neither a superset nor a plain exercise.
  CHECK ((group_index IS NULL AND group_kind IS NULL) OR (group_index IS NOT NULL AND group_kind IS NOT NULL)),
  -- The discriminator must actually discriminate: the player has to have something to render.
  CHECK (
    (prescription_kind = 'reps'     AND target_reps_min IS NOT NULL) OR
    (prescription_kind = 'time'     AND target_duration_seconds IS NOT NULL) OR
    (prescription_kind = 'distance' AND target_distance_m IS NOT NULL)
  )
);

-- The player and the editor both read a day in order.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_plan_items_day ON workout_plan_items (day_id, position);
-- Backs the exercise-grant check and "which plans use this exercise" before a coach deletes it.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_plan_items_exercise ON workout_plan_items (exercise_id);

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_workout_plan_items_touch
AFTER UPDATE ON workout_plan_items FOR EACH ROW
WHEN NEW.updated_at = OLD.updated_at
BEGIN
  UPDATE workout_plan_items SET updated_at = unixepoch() WHERE id = NEW.id;
END;

tables.name: workout_plan_item_sets
tables.purpose: Optional per-set prescription, for anything the flat item cannot express: a 5/5/3/3/1 wave, a top set with backoffs, warm-up ramps, a terminal AMRAP. When absent, session materialisation expands the item's flat prescription into `target_sets` identical rows — so the player only ever consumes one shape.
tables.ddl:
-- The player materialises a row per SET regardless, so having a per-set prescription source is
-- symmetric rather than extra: absent rows mean "repeat the flat prescription target_sets times".
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_plan_item_sets (
  id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  item_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_plan_items(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  set_number INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (set_number BETWEEN 1 AND 20),
  -- 'warmup' is load-bearing, not cosmetic: a warm-up set is excluded from PR evaluation.
  set_kind   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal'
             CHECK (set_kind IN ('normal', 'warmup', 'drop', 'backoff', 'amrap', 'failure')),
  target_reps     INTEGER CHECK (target_reps IS NULL OR target_reps BETWEEN 1 AND 200),
  target_weight_kg REAL CHECK (target_weight_kg IS NULL OR (target_weight_kg >= 0 AND target_weight_kg <= 1000)),
  target_percent_1rm INTEGER CHECK (target_percent_1rm IS NULL OR target_percent_1rm BETWEEN 10 AND 150),
  target_duration_seconds INTEGER CHECK (target_duration_seconds IS NULL OR target_duration_seconds BETWEEN 1 AND 36000),
  target_distance_m INTEGER CHECK (target_distance_m IS NULL OR target_distance_m BETWEEN 1 AND 200000),
  target_rpe   REAL CHECK (target_rpe IS NULL OR (target_rpe >= 1 AND target_rpe <= 10)),
  rest_seconds INTEGER CHECK (rest_seconds IS NULL OR rest_seconds BETWEEN 0 AND 3600),
  -- Two prescriptions for set 3 would give the player two truths to choose from.
  UNIQUE (item_id, set_number)
);

tables.name: workout_plan_translations
tables.purpose: Translated title/description for product-shipped stock templates (owner_id NULL). Coach-authored plan titles are prose in the coach's own language and are deliberately NOT translated — the same call onboarding made for `notes`. Shape copied verbatim from taxonomy_translations so there is one i18n pattern, not two.
tables.ddl:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_plan_translations (
  id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  plan_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_plans(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  lang    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES languages(code) ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  title   TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(title)) BETWEEN 1 AND 120),
  description TEXT CHECK (description IS NULL OR length(description) <= 2000),
  origin  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'manual' CHECK (origin IN ('manual', 'dataset', 'machine')),
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  -- One title per language, or the picker chooses at random.
  UNIQUE (plan_id, lang)
);

-- Rowid table with a surrogate id, matching exercise_translations: if stock templates ever need
-- FTS5 external content, a WITHOUT ROWID table could not carry the index.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_plan_tr_lookup ON workout_plan_translations (lang, plan_id);

tables.name: workout_logs
tables.purpose: One training session. `plan_id`/`plan_day_id` are nullable SET NULL breadcrumbs, never dependencies — a freestyle session is this same row with two NULLs and source='freestyle'. `client_uid` is client-minted so a session can be created while offline and reconciled exactly once. A partial unique index enforces one active session per user, which is what makes "resume my workout" a single unambiguous row.
tables.ddl:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_logs (
  id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- Client-minted ULID. The player must be able to start a session with no network, address
  -- every subsequent op against it, and have the server adopt it exactly once on reconnect.
  client_uid TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(client_uid) BETWEEN 16 AND 64),

  -- Breadcrumbs, not dependencies. Nothing in the execution path joins through these; the plan
  -- is read ONCE, at materialisation, and never again. SET NULL so deleting a plan cannot take
  -- the history with it.
  plan_id      INTEGER REFERENCES workout_plans(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  plan_day_id  INTEGER REFERENCES workout_plan_days(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  plan_version INTEGER,

  title  TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(title)) BETWEEN 1 AND 120),
  source TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'plan' CHECK (source IN ('plan', 'freestyle', 'repeat')),

  -- The civil date the plan prescribed (NULL for freestyle) and the civil date the client was
  -- actually living in. Adherence compares the two; both are dates, not instants, so a session
  -- at 23:40 in Sydney is not yesterday's workout.
  scheduled_date TEXT CHECK (scheduled_date IS NULL OR scheduled_date GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]'),
  local_date     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (local_date GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]'),

  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active', 'finished', 'abandoned')),

  -- started_at is SERVER time and is what orders history. client_started_at is the client's own
  -- clock, kept for display only — a forged timestamp must not be able to reorder a record book.
  started_at        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  client_started_at INTEGER,
  finished_at       INTEGER,
  last_activity_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),

  -- Server-computed rollups. Never accepted from the client, always recomputed by aggregate.
  duration_seconds INTEGER CHECK (duration_seconds IS NULL OR duration_seconds BETWEEN 0 AND 86400),
  total_sets       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (total_sets >= 0),
  total_reps       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (total_reps >= 0),
  total_volume_kg  REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (total_volume_kg >= 0),
  exercise_count   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (exercise_count >= 0),
  pr_count         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (pr_count >= 0),

  perceived_effort INTEGER CHECK (perceived_effort IS NULL OR perceived_effort BETWEEN 1 AND 10),
  notes TEXT CHECK (notes IS NULL OR length(notes) <= 2000),

  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),

  CHECK (status <> 'finished' OR finished_at IS NOT NULL)
);

-- Exactly-once session creation from an offline queue. This index is the whole offline story.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_logs_client_uid ON workout_logs (user_id, client_uid);
-- One active session per user: "resume" is then a single row, and a second device cannot fork it.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_logs_one_active ON workout_logs (user_id) WHERE status = 'active';
-- History list, and the coach's client-detail feed.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_logs_user_recent ON workout_logs (user_id, started_at DESC);
-- Home card + adherence ring: "did I already train on this date".
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_logs_user_date ON workout_logs (user_id, local_date);
-- "has this prescribed day been done", for the week strip.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_logs_plan_day ON workout_logs (plan_day_id, status);
-- The stale-session sweeper.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_logs_stale ON workout_logs (last_activity_at) WHERE status = 'active';

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_workout_logs_touch
AFTER UPDATE ON workout_logs FOR EACH ROW
WHEN NEW.updated_at = OLD.updated_at
BEGIN
  UPDATE workout_logs SET updated_at = unixepoch() WHERE id = NEW.id;
END;

tables.name: workout_log_entries
tables.purpose: One exercise inside one session, and the home of `prev_entry_id` — THE previous-performance pointer, resolved once at materialisation and then immutable. It also carries the per-exercise rollups that the progress graph reads directly, so a graph is an indexed range scan with no aggregation. `exercise_name_snapshot` + `ON DELETE SET NULL` mean history renders forever, even after the coach who owned the exercise deletes their account.
tables.ddl:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_log_entries (
  id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  log_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_logs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- Denormalised from the parent. Every ownership scope and every history index hits this table
  -- directly instead of joining up to workout_logs; a trigger below makes the copy unforgeable.
  user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  client_uid TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(client_uid) BETWEEN 16 AND 64),

  -- SET NULL, not CASCADE: a coach account deletion cascades their private exercises away, and
  -- that must not erase a client's training history. The snapshot is what keeps it readable.
  exercise_id INTEGER REFERENCES exercises(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  exercise_name_snapshot TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(exercise_name_snapshot)) BETWEEN 1 AND 200),
  plan_item_id INTEGER REFERENCES workout_plan_items(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,

  position    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (position >= 0),
  group_index INTEGER CHECK (group_index IS NULL OR group_index BETWEEN 0 AND 50),
  group_kind  TEXT CHECK (group_kind IS NULL OR group_kind IN ('superset', 'circuit')),
  prescription_kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'reps' CHECK (prescription_kind IN ('reps', 'time', 'distance')),

  -- 'plan' came from the prescription, 'added' is the client freestyling mid-session,
  -- 'substituted' is the client swapping an exercise they could not do today.
  origin TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'plan' CHECK (origin IN ('plan', 'added', 'substituted')),
  substituted_for_exercise_id INTEGER REFERENCES exercises(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,

  -- ── THE previous-performance pointer ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  -- Resolved ONCE, inside the transaction that materialises the session, and then frozen. The
  -- player fetches every "prev" cell for the whole workout with one indexed join instead of one
  -- correlated latest-per-group query per set row. Freezing it also makes it history: the prev
  -- shown next year is the prev that was shown on the day.
  prev_entry_id INTEGER REFERENCES workout_log_entries(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,

  -- Server clock, copied from workout_logs.started_at. Orders the record book.
  performed_at       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  -- Set once, on the first completed set. Set-once so the partial index below never churns.
  first_completed_at INTEGER,

  -- Per-exercise rollups, recomputed by aggregate on every accepted set write. The progress
  -- graph reads these columns straight off this index — no GROUP BY on the read path.
  completed_sets  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (completed_sets >= 0),
  total_reps      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (total_reps >= 0),
  total_volume_kg REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (total_volume_kg >= 0),
  top_weight_kg   REAL,
  top_est_1rm_kg  REAL,
  top_duration_seconds INTEGER,

  notes TEXT CHECK (notes IS NULL OR length(notes) <= 1000),
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),

  CHECK ((group_index IS NULL AND group_kind IS NULL) OR (group_index IS NOT NULL AND group_kind IS NOT NULL)),
  CHECK (origin <> 'substituted' OR substituted_for_exercise_id IS NOT NULL)
);

-- Exactly-once entry creation from the offline queue.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_log_entries_uid ON workout_log_entries (log_id, client_uid);
-- The player loads a session in order.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_log_entries_log ON workout_log_entries (log_id, position);

-- THE history index. It serves three of the busiest reads in the product with one structure:
--   1. resolving prev_entry_id at materialisation (LIMIT 1 off the front),
--   2. the per-exercise progress graph (a range scan, columns already aggregated),
--   3. a records recompute after an edit.
-- Partial on first_completed_at so an opened-and-skipped exercise never becomes "last time".
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_log_entries_history
  ON workout_log_entries (user_id, exercise_id, performed_at DESC, id DESC)
  WHERE first_completed_at IS NOT NULL;

-- Lets a delete find the entries pointing at the deleted one.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_log_entries_prev ON workout_log_entries (prev_entry_id);

-- The denormalised user_id is only safe if it cannot disagree with the parent.
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_workout_log_entries_parent
BEFORE INSERT ON workout_log_entries FOR EACH ROW
WHEN (SELECT user_id FROM workout_logs WHERE id = NEW.log_id) IS NOT NEW.user_id
BEGIN
  SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'workout_log_entries.user_id must match its log');
END;

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_workout_log_entries_touch
AFTER UPDATE ON workout_log_entries FOR EACH ROW
WHEN NEW.updated_at = OLD.updated_at
BEGIN
  UPDATE workout_log_entries SET updated_at = unixepoch() WHERE id = NEW.id;
END;

tables.name: workout_log_sets
tables.purpose: The hot table and the heart of the design. Set rows are materialised as 'pending' when the session starts, carrying a full snapshot of their prescription — so the player, the rest timer and the offline queue need nothing from the plan. Checking a set is a guarded UPDATE with a monotonic client sequence in the WHERE clause. `volume_kg` and `est_1rm_kg` are VIRTUAL generated columns, which makes it physically impossible for a client to submit a derived value.
tables.ddl:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_log_sets (
  id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  entry_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_log_entries(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- Both parents denormalised: log_id so a whole session's sets are one indexed scan, user_id so
  -- the hottest write in the product needs no join to prove ownership. A trigger keeps them true.
  log_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_logs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  client_uid TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(client_uid) BETWEEN 16 AND 64),

  set_number INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (set_number BETWEEN 1 AND 50),
  set_kind   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal'
             CHECK (set_kind IN ('normal', 'warmup', 'drop', 'backoff', 'amrap', 'failure')),
  -- 'pending' rows exist from the moment the session is materialised; that is what makes the
  -- check a guarded UPDATE rather than an INSERT, and an INSERT is what double-taps duplicate.
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'done', 'skipped', 'voided')),

  -- ── prescription SNAPSHOT, frozen at materialisation ────────────────────────────────────
  -- The plan may be edited or deleted under a running session; this row does not care.
  target_reps       INTEGER CHECK (target_reps IS NULL OR target_reps BETWEEN 1 AND 200),
  target_weight_kg  REAL CHECK (target_weight_kg IS NULL OR (target_weight_kg >= 0 AND target_weight_kg <= 1000)),
  target_duration_seconds INTEGER CHECK (target_duration_seconds IS NULL OR target_duration_seconds BETWEEN 1 AND 36000),
  target_distance_m INTEGER CHECK (target_distance_m IS NULL OR target_distance_m BETWEEN 1 AND 200000),
  target_rpe        REAL CHECK (target_rpe IS NULL OR (target_rpe >= 1 AND target_rpe <= 10)),
  target_rest_seconds INTEGER CHECK (target_rest_seconds IS NULL OR target_rest_seconds BETWEEN 0 AND 3600),

  -- ── what the client OBSERVED. Raw observations are the one thing that legitimately comes
  -- from the client; everything derived from them is computed here.
  weight_kg REAL    CHECK (weight_kg IS NULL OR (weight_kg >= 0 AND weight_kg <= 1000)),
  reps      INTEGER CHECK (reps IS NULL OR reps BETWEEN 0 AND 500),
  duration_seconds INTEGER CHECK (duration_seconds IS NULL OR duration_seconds BETWEEN 0 AND 36000),
  distance_m INTEGER CHECK (distance_m IS NULL OR distance_m BETWEEN 0 AND 200000),
  rpe       REAL    CHECK (rpe IS NULL OR (rpe >= 1 AND rpe <= 10)),
  rest_taken_seconds INTEGER CHECK (rest_taken_seconds IS NULL OR rest_taken_seconds BETWEEN 0 AND 3600),

  -- ── SERVER-DERIVED, and unwritable by construction ──────────────────────────────────────
  -- A generated column has no INSERT/UPDATE surface at all: there is no code path, forged or
  -- otherwise, that can put a client-supplied 1RM into this database. Gated on status so
  -- voiding a set removes its contribution automatically.
  volume_kg REAL GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
    CASE WHEN status = 'done' AND weight_kg IS NOT NULL AND reps IS NOT NULL
         THEN weight_kg * reps END
  ) VIRTUAL,
  -- Epley, capped at 12 reps: above that the formula is fiction, and an unbounded Epley lets a
  -- 40-rep bodyweight set manufacture a strength PR.
  est_1rm_kg REAL GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
    CASE WHEN status = 'done' AND weight_kg > 0 AND reps BETWEEN 1 AND 12
         THEN weight_kg * (1 + reps / 30.0) END
  ) VIRTUAL,

  completed_at        INTEGER,  -- server clock
  client_completed_at INTEGER,  -- the client's clock, for an offline set. Display only.

  -- ── IDEMPOTENCY ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  -- A per-session monotonic counter minted by the player and persisted beside its offline
  -- queue. The guard `? > last_client_seq` lives INSIDE the UPDATE, so a replayed or
  -- out-of-order delivery changes zero rows and every downstream effect is skipped.
  last_client_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (last_client_seq >= 0),
  -- The op that last won, for debugging and for echoing `replayed` honestly to the client.
  last_op_id TEXT CHECK (last_op_id IS NULL OR length(last_op_id) BETWEEN 8 AND 64),

  notes TEXT CHECK (notes IS NULL OR length(notes) <= 500),
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),

  CHECK (status <> 'done' OR completed_at IS NOT NULL)
);

-- Exactly-once set creation from the offline queue (an ad-hoc set added while disconnected).
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_log_sets_uid ON workout_log_sets (entry_id, client_uid);
-- Two rows for set 3 would make "previous performance for set 3" ambiguous. This UNIQUE index is
-- also the ordered read path the player and the prev-performance fetch both use.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_log_sets_number ON workout_log_sets (entry_id, set_number);
-- Session-wide reads: the finish-summary rollup and the "n of m sets done" chip.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_log_sets_log ON workout_log_sets (log_id, status);

-- The denormalised parents are only safe if they cannot disagree.
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_workout_log_sets_parent
BEFORE INSERT ON workout_log_sets FOR EACH ROW
WHEN (SELECT e.log_id || ':' || e.user_id FROM workout_log_entries e WHERE e.id = NEW.entry_id)
     IS NOT (NEW.log_id || ':' || NEW.user_id)
BEGIN
  SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'workout_log_sets: log_id/user_id must match its entry');
END;

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_workout_log_sets_touch
AFTER UPDATE ON workout_log_sets FOR EACH ROW
WHEN NEW.updated_at = OLD.updated_at
BEGIN
  UPDATE workout_log_sets SET updated_at = unixepoch() WHERE id = NEW.id;
END;

tables.name: exercise_records
tables.purpose: The current record book: one row per (user, exercise) holding every current best plus lifetime totals. It exists so PR detection is a comparison against ONE row inside the write transaction instead of a scan of history while holding SQLite's single write lock. It is explicitly a CACHE with a deterministic rebuild path, flagged by `needs_recompute` when an edit invalidates it.
tables.ddl:
-- A derived table, and honest about it. The justification is the write lock: SQLite has exactly
-- one writer, so a PR check that scans a client's history is a scan every other writer in the
-- process waits behind. Comparing against one indexed row is not.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS exercise_records (
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- CASCADE: a cache row for an exercise that no longer exists is garbage. History survives
  -- regardless, via workout_log_entries.exercise_name_snapshot.
  exercise_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES exercises(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

  best_weight_kg     REAL,
  best_weight_reps   INTEGER,
  best_weight_set_id INTEGER REFERENCES workout_log_sets(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  best_weight_at     INTEGER,

  best_reps           INTEGER,
  best_reps_weight_kg REAL,
  best_reps_set_id    INTEGER REFERENCES workout_log_sets(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  best_reps_at        INTEGER,

  best_est_1rm_kg     REAL,
  best_est_1rm_set_id INTEGER REFERENCES workout_log_sets(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  best_est_1rm_at     INTEGER,

  best_duration_seconds INTEGER,
  best_duration_set_id  INTEGER REFERENCES workout_log_sets(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  best_duration_at      INTEGER,

  best_distance_m       INTEGER,
  best_distance_set_id  INTEGER REFERENCES workout_log_sets(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  best_distance_at      INTEGER,

  best_session_volume_kg REAL,
  best_session_entry_id  INTEGER REFERENCES workout_log_entries(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  best_session_at        INTEGER,

  -- Lifetime counters. Rolled up ONCE per session, at finish, guarded by the status transition —
  -- never incremented per set, because an increment is exactly what a replay double-counts.
  session_count   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (session_count >= 0),
  total_sets      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (total_sets >= 0),
  total_reps      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (total_reps >= 0),
  total_volume_kg REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (total_volume_kg >= 0),
  last_performed_at INTEGER,

  -- Set when an EDIT lowers the very set that holds a record. Recomputing the record book inline
  -- would make the rare case pay for by the common one; the read path sees the flag and calls
  -- recomputeExerciseRecords() in its own transaction.
  needs_recompute INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (needs_recompute IN (0, 1)),
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),

  -- Rowid table + UNIQUE rather than a WITHOUT ROWID composite PK: this row is thick with
  -- scalar payload, and the 007/008 precedent for a composite natural key is exactly this shape.
  UNIQUE (user_id, exercise_id)
);

-- The "my records" screen, most recent first.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_exercise_records_user ON exercise_records (user_id, last_performed_at DESC);
-- The repair queue.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_exercise_records_stale ON exercise_records (needs_recompute) WHERE needs_recompute = 1;

tables.name: workout_prs
tables.purpose: The PR event log — what the gold badge, the notification and the (future) coin reward all read. Separate from exercise_records because a record is a current value while a PR is a moment in time. The two partial UNIQUE indexes are the database-level backstop that makes a double-counted PR structurally impossible even if the transaction logic is wrong.
tables.ddl:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_prs (
  id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- SET NULL: the PR happened even if the exercise is later deleted.
  exercise_id  INTEGER REFERENCES exercises(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  log_id       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_logs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  log_entry_id INTEGER REFERENCES workout_log_entries(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- NULL for a session-scoped PR (best volume for this exercise in one session).
  log_set_id   INTEGER REFERENCES workout_log_sets(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

  kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('weight', 'reps', 'est-1rm', 'duration', 'distance', 'session-volume')),
  value          REAL NOT NULL,
  previous_value REAL,           -- NULL = the first ever, which the UI phrases differently
  weight_kg      REAL,
  reps           INTEGER,
  achieved_at    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  -- Set when a later PR of the same kind beats it. Kept rather than deleted: the graph of
  -- "every time I broke this record" is the point.
  superseded_at  INTEGER,
  -- Set when an edit invalidates it. A revoked PR is not a deleted one — a badge that was shown
  -- and then withdrawn is a thing the client is owed an explanation for.
  revoked_at     INTEGER,

  -- The hook Phase 7's coin economy plugs into, without inventing the economy here. A reward is
  -- granted against a PR ROW, and the unique indexes below make that row unique per set+kind —
  -- so "a replayed set check must not double-award" is enforced by the same constraint that
  -- stops it double-counting the PR.
  reward_state      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (reward_state IN ('pending', 'granted', 'skipped')),
  reward_granted_at INTEGER,

  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),

  CHECK (kind = 'session-volume' OR log_set_id IS NOT NULL),
  CHECK (kind <> 'session-volume' OR (log_set_id IS NULL AND log_entry_id IS NOT NULL))
);

-- THE backstop. One PR of a given kind per set, enforced by the database rather than by the
-- correctness of the transaction above it. NULLs are distinct in a SQLite UNIQUE index, so the
-- set-scoped and entry-scoped cases need two partial indexes rather than one.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_prs_set_kind
  ON workout_prs (log_set_id, kind) WHERE log_set_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_prs_entry_kind
  ON workout_prs (log_entry_id, kind) WHERE log_set_id IS NULL;

-- The "recent PRs" strip on the home screen and the coach's client feed.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_prs_user ON workout_prs (user_id, achieved_at DESC);
-- The per-exercise record history that the progress graph overlays as markers.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_prs_exercise ON workout_prs (user_id, exercise_id, kind, achieved_at DESC);
-- The reward worker's queue.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_prs_reward ON workout_prs (reward_state) WHERE reward_state = 'pending';

tables.name: workout_exercise_grants
tables.purpose: Fixes the hole the ground truth found: `exercises` are visible only when global or self-owned, so a coach's private exercise placed in a client's plan would 404 for that client. A grant is an explicit capability row, written when the exercise enters the client's plan or log, and DELETEd when the coach archives the link — so an archived coach's private library is re-hidden, while history still reads from the name snapshot.
tables.ddl:
-- A capability, not a cache of a derived query. Extending the VISIBLE predicate with an EXISTS
-- over coach_clients was the alternative and it is wrong: it would expose a coach's ENTIRE
-- private library — including unfinished drafts — to every client who searches for "curl".
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_exercise_grants (
  user_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  exercise_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES exercises(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- Who exposed it. CASCADE because if the granting coach is gone their private exercises are
  -- gone with them, and revoking on archive is DELETE ... WHERE granted_by = ?.
  granted_by  INTEGER REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, exercise_id)
) WITHOUT ROWID;

-- WITHOUT ROWID because the read is always the exact PK — this table is probed once per
-- non-global exercise on the busiest screen — and it will never carry an FTS5 external-content
-- index, which is the one thing that would forbid it (004_translations.sql:12-15).

-- The revoke-on-archive path, and the coach's "who can see my exercise" answer.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workout_exercise_grants_by ON workout_exercise_grants (granted_by, user_id);

tables.name: body_area_muscle_map
tables.purpose: The missing join that makes T2.5.4 ("suggestions filtered by the client's avoid-list") implementable. `onboarding_limitations.body_area` is joint-centric ('knee', 'wrist') while exercises are tagged by muscle group — nothing connected the two. A seeded, admin-editable junction, not a JSON list and not a CHECK.

tables.name: calendar_feed_tokens
tables.purpose: ICS export needs an authentication mechanism that calendar apps actually have — and Google Calendar cannot send an HttpOnly cookie. A hashed, revocable, per-user feed token, shaped exactly like invite_codes: shown in plaintext once, stored as a SHA-256 hash, never recoverable from a database leak.
tables.ddl:
-- Without this table "ICS export" quietly becomes either a download button (which never updates)
-- or an unauthenticated URL. A subscribable webcal:// feed needs a bearer secret in the URL, and
-- a bearer secret in a URL must be revocable and must not be stored in the clear.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS calendar_feed_tokens (
  id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- NULL = every plan this user can see. Non-NULL scopes the feed to one plan.
  plan_id INTEGER REFERENCES workout_plans(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  token_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  label      TEXT CHECK (label IS NULL OR length(trim(label)) BETWEEN 1 AND 40),
  revoked_at   INTEGER,
  last_used_at INTEGER,
  created_at   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_calendar_feed_tokens_hash ON calendar_feed_tokens (token_hash);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_calendar_feed_tokens_user ON calendar_feed_tokens (user_id, revoked_at);

keyDecisions.decision: `prev_entry_id` is a real column on `workout_log_entries`, resolved once when the session is materialised and then frozen forever.
keyDecisions.rationale: "Previous performance" is the busiest read in the product — one cell per set, per exercise, per session. As a pointer it collapses to ONE query for the entire workout: `SELECT s.* FROM workout_log_entries cur JOIN workout_log_sets s ON s.entry_id = cur.prev_entry_id WHERE cur.log_id = ?`. Resolving it costs one `LIMIT 1` off `idx_workout_log_entries_history` per exercise, paid once at session start when the client is standing still, not once per set row while they are training. Freezing it also makes it history: the 'prev' the client saw on the day is the 'prev' the log still shows next year.
keyDecisions.rejected: (a) A correlated latest-per-group query per set row — 20-40 separate pool tasks per session open, each landing on a different worker connection. (b) One window-function query per session (`ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY exercise_id ORDER BY performed_at DESC)`) — correct and only one query, but it re-derives on every page load, gets slower as history grows, and gives a DIFFERENT answer once a backfilled session appears, silently rewriting what a past workout claimed to be improving on. (c) A JSON snapshot of the previous sets on the entry — forbidden by the rules and unqueryable.

keyDecisions.decision: Every rollup is RECOMPUTED by aggregate, never incremented.
keyDecisions.rationale: `completed_sets`, `total_reps`, `total_volume_kg`, `top_weight_kg` and `top_est_1rm_kg` on the entry are all written as `= (SELECT ... FROM workout_log_sets WHERE entry_id = ? AND status = 'done')`. A recompute is idempotent by construction: run it twice, get the same number. An increment (`total_reps = total_reps + ?`) is the exact statement that double-counts the moment any replay slips past the guard. This is the second, independent layer of the idempotency story and it costs a scan of ~5 rows.
keyDecisions.rejected: Incremental deltas. They are cheaper, but their correctness depends entirely on the guard above them never failing — and the guard depends on the client's sequence counter, which is the one input we do not control. Two mechanisms that fail independently are worth 5 extra row reads.

keyDecisions.decision: `volume_kg` and `est_1rm_kg` are VIRTUAL GENERATED columns, not columns the write path fills in.
keyDecisions.rationale: The rule is "every authoritative value is computed on the backend". A generated column is stronger than a convention: it has no INSERT or UPDATE surface at all, so there is no code path — forged, refactored, or written by a future contributor in a hurry — that can put a client-supplied 1RM into this database. Gating both expressions on `status = 'done'` means voiding a set removes its contribution automatically, and the entry rollup self-heals on the next recompute. Epley is capped at 12 reps because above that the formula is fiction and an uncapped one lets a 40-rep bodyweight set manufacture a strength PR.
keyDecisions.rejected: Computing them in the worker and storing them as plain REAL columns. Identical arithmetic, but it relies on every write path remembering — and the repo's own history (ADR-0005) is a story about exactly that kind of forgetting. A STORED generated column was also rejected: VIRTUAL costs no bytes and is still indexable.

keyDecisions.decision: Idempotency is a monotonic `last_client_seq` guard inside the UPDATE, not an `idempotency_keys` table.
keyDecisions.rationale: One INTEGER column on the row it protects. It is self-GCing (no expiry job), it costs no extra write, and — critically — it is order-INSENSITIVE, so an offline queue that replays out of order still converges: the highest sequence wins and every stale delivery changes zero rows. It also covers the case a naive dedupe misses: a set EDITED twice offline, where replaying the queue with a plain 'have I seen this op id' check would re-apply the older correction.
keyDecisions.rejected: (a) A generic `idempotency_keys(user_id, key, response)` table: it needs a GC job, it stores response bodies that drift from the truth, and it adds a second write to the hottest path in the product. (b) A bare `last_op_id` equality check: correct for retries, but an A→B→A replay re-applies A. `last_op_id` is kept anyway, but only so the response can honestly say WHICH op won.

keyDecisions.decision: The whole session — log, entries and sets — carries a client-minted `client_uid`, with a UNIQUE index per parent.
keyDecisions.rationale: This is what makes the mid-workout connectivity loss a non-event. The player mints the session id itself, addresses every queued operation against uids rather than server ids, and needs no round trip until it reconnects. On reconnect one call replays the queue in one IMMEDIATE transaction; creation is `ON CONFLICT (user_id, client_uid) DO NOTHING` so a session is adopted exactly once no matter how many times the flush is retried. Three TEXT columns and three unique indexes buy a genuinely offline-first player.
keyDecisions.rejected: Server-assigned ids with a client-side id-mapping table. It works, but it forces a round trip before the client can log its first set, which is precisely the moment the gym basement has no signal.

keyDecisions.decision: The session is a SNAPSHOT taken at start. Every set row carries its own prescription; the plan is read once, at materialisation, and never again.
keyDecisions.rationale: It solves three problems with one move. (1) A log cannot change retroactively — a coach editing the plan tonight cannot alter what yesterday's log claims was prescribed. (2) A coach editing the plan while the client is mid-set does not mutate the running session; the edit lands on the next one. (3) The player has everything it needs to run offline, including the rest-timer duration, without caching the plan separately. `plan_id`/`plan_day_id`/`plan_item_id` are all nullable ON DELETE SET NULL, so deleting a plan degrades a log to 'orphaned but complete', never to 'broken'.
keyDecisions.rejected: Reading the prescription through a live join to `workout_plan_items` on every render. Cheaper in storage, and completely wrong: it makes history a view of mutable data, and it makes a plan delete a history delete.

keyDecisions.decision: A freestyle workout is the same row with NULLs, and `workout_exercise_grants` decouples exercise visibility from the plan.
keyDecisions.rationale: Off-plan is first-class because nothing in the execution path depends on a plan being present: entries carry `exercise_id` + `exercise_name_snapshot` directly, sets carry their own targets (or none), and `origin` distinguishes 'plan' / 'added' / 'substituted'. Separately, the grant table fixes the visibility hole: `exercises/routes.js:26` makes a coach's private exercise invisible to their own client, so a plan built from a coach's custom library would 404 for the person meant to perform it. The grant is written when the exercise enters the client's world and DELETEd when the coach archives the link, so archiving re-hides the coach's library while history still reads from the name snapshot.
keyDecisions.rejected: Extending the VISIBLE predicate with an EXISTS over `coach_clients` — that hands a client the coach's ENTIRE private library, drafts and all, the first time they type into the search box. Also rejected: snapshotting the full exercise (name, media, muscles) into every plan item, which would fork 1652 rows of curated content into thousands of stale copies.

keyDecisions.decision: Scheduled days are civil TEXT dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`), deliberately breaking the epoch-seconds convention.
keyDecisions.rationale: The epoch rule governs instants; a scheduled day is not an instant. A workout prescribed for Tuesday must stay on Tuesday when the client flies to Denver, and an epoch would silently slide it. `workout_logs` therefore carries `scheduled_date` (what the plan said) and `local_date` (the civil date the client was actually living in) alongside `started_at` (a real, server-clock instant that orders the record book). Adherence compares the two dates; history orders by the instant. Conflating them is how a 23:40 session in Sydney gets counted as yesterday's.
keyDecisions.rejected: Epoch-of-local-midnight. It looks like it obeys the convention while being a worse date: it is only correct for one timezone, and nothing in the type tells you which.

keyDecisions.decision: `exercise_records` is a declared cache with a `needs_recompute` flag, not a derive-on-read view.
keyDecisions.rationale: SQLite has exactly one writer. A PR check that scans a client's history for that exercise is a scan every other writer in the process queues behind, inside the write lock, on the hottest endpoint in the product. Comparing against one indexed row is not. When an edit lowers the very set that holds a record — rare — the transaction sets `needs_recompute = 1` instead of paying for a rebuild inline, and the read path repairs it in its own transaction.
keyDecisions.rejected: Deriving records on read with MAX() over history. Honest, always correct, and it turns every progress screen into a full-history aggregate. Also rejected: making the recompute part of the set-check transaction, which makes the common path pay the rare path's cost.

keyDecisions.decision: Six named worker transactions, and a corresponding line in `src/db/index.js` for each. The app currently has zero.
keyDecisions.rationale: `writeTx` cannot read, branch, or inspect an intermediate result (`worker.js:97-99`), so none of PR detection, prev-pointer resolution, session materialisation, or plan cloning is expressible with it. The mechanism exists (Piscina `{ name }`) but is unexercised outside `migrate`, so the design has to name both halves or it is not implementable: `startWorkoutSession`, `logSetOp`, `syncOfflineQueue`, `finishWorkoutSession`, `clonePlan` (covers copy-day and copy-week), `recomputeExerciseRecords`. Every one obeys ADR-0005: all error-producing validation runs before the first write, and any post-write failure `throw`s a typed error rather than returning one.
keyDecisions.rejected: Chaining several `db.run` calls from the route. Each is its own autocommit transaction on a possibly different connection — a set check would be four separate commits, and a crash between them leaves a PR awarded against a set that was never marked done.

designs.idempotency:
Four independent layers, in the order a replay hits them. All of it lives inside ONE named worker transaction (`logSetOp`), running `tx.immediate()`.

LAYER 0 — the row already exists. Set rows are materialised as `status='pending'` when the session starts, so checking a set is an UPDATE, never an INSERT. There is no statement in the hot path that can create a duplicate row, which is what a double-tapped INSERT would do.

LAYER 1 — existence + ownership, before any write (ADR-0005 compliance):
  SELECT s.id, s.status, s.last_client_seq, s.set_kind, e.exercise_id
    FROM workout_log_sets s
    JOIN workout_logs l ON l.id = s.log_id
   WHERE s.id = ? AND s.user_id = ? AND l.status = 'active';
