No row → `throw NotFound` → the tx rolls back having written nothing, and the route maps it to 404 (never 403). This is NOT a select-then-update race: the transaction is IMMEDIATE, so the write lock is already held and nothing can change underneath it. The guard still lives in the UPDATE below, because that is what keeps the write self-defending if it is ever refactored out of a transaction.

LAYER 2 — the monotonic guard, INSIDE the UPDATE. `:seq` is the player's per-session counter, persisted beside its offline queue:
  UPDATE workout_log_sets
     SET status = 'done', weight_kg = :w, reps = :r, duration_seconds = :d,
         rpe = :rpe, rest_taken_seconds = :rest,
         completed_at = COALESCE(completed_at, unixepoch()),
         client_completed_at = :clientTs,
         last_client_seq = :seq, last_op_id = :opId
   WHERE id = :id AND user_id = :me AND :seq > last_client_seq;
`changes = 0` means a replay, a double tap, or an out-of-order delivery from the offline queue. The function returns `{ replayed: 1, set: <current row> }` and NOTHING below runs. `changes = 0` here is deliberately NOT an error — a double-tapped check is the client's most ordinary mistake (`onboarding/routes.js:237-244` set that precedent). Returning after a zero-change UPDATE is ADR-0005-safe precisely because no write happened.

LAYER 3 — rollups by aggregate, never by increment. Only reached when `changes = 1`:
  UPDATE workout_log_entries SET
    completed_sets     = (SELECT COUNT(*)                FROM workout_log_sets WHERE entry_id = :e AND status = 'done'),
    total_reps         = (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(reps), 0)  FROM workout_log_sets WHERE entry_id = :e AND status = 'done'),
    total_volume_kg    = (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(volume_kg), 0) FROM workout_log_sets WHERE entry_id = :e),
    top_weight_kg      = (SELECT MAX(weight_kg)          FROM workout_log_sets WHERE entry_id = :e AND status = 'done'),
    top_est_1rm_kg     = (SELECT MAX(est_1rm_kg)         FROM workout_log_sets WHERE entry_id = :e),
    first_completed_at = COALESCE(first_completed_at, unixepoch())
  WHERE id = :e AND user_id = :me;
Even if layers 1–2 were bypassed entirely, running this twice produces the same numbers. `volume_kg`/`est_1rm_kg` are the generated columns, which self-null for non-'done' rows.

LAYER 4 — the PR, guarded three ways at once: by the comparison, by the `changes = 1` gate above it, and by a UNIQUE index the transaction cannot talk its way past:
  INSERT INTO workout_prs (user_id, exercise_id, log_id, log_entry_id, log_set_id, kind,
                           value, previous_value, weight_kg, reps, achieved_at)
  SELECT s.user_id, e.exercise_id, s.log_id, s.entry_id, s.id, 'est-1rm',
         s.est_1rm_kg, r.best_est_1rm_kg, s.weight_kg, s.reps, unixepoch()
    FROM workout_log_sets s
    JOIN workout_log_entries e ON e.id = s.entry_id
    LEFT JOIN exercise_records r ON r.user_id = s.user_id AND r.exercise_id = e.exercise_id
   WHERE s.id = :id
     AND s.status = 'done'
     AND s.set_kind <> 'warmup'
     AND s.est_1rm_kg IS NOT NULL
     AND (r.best_est_1rm_kg IS NULL OR s.est_1rm_kg > r.best_est_1rm_kg)
  ON CONFLICT (log_set_id, kind) WHERE log_set_id IS NOT NULL DO NOTHING;
Two things make this un-double-countable. (i) `idx_workout_prs_set_kind` is UNIQUE on `(log_set_id, kind)` — a second PR row for the same set and kind is refused by the database, not by the code. The conflict target repeats the partial index's WHERE clause, as SQLite requires. (ii) the comparison is a STRICT `>` against the cached record, and the record is advanced in the same transaction — so even a hypothetical second pass sees `est_1rm_kg > best_est_1rm_kg` as false. Epley on identical (weight, reps) inputs is bit-identical, so equality holds and no epsilon is needed. Since a coin reward is granted against a `workout_prs` ROW (`reward_state`), the same UNIQUE index that stops a double PR stops a double award — one constraint, both requirements.

LAYER 5 — the record cache, upserted with idempotent operators:
  INSERT INTO exercise_records (user_id, exercise_id, best_est_1rm_kg, best_est_1rm_set_id, best_est_1rm_at, updated_at)
  VALUES (:me, :ex, :v, :setId, unixepoch(), unixepoch())
  ON CONFLICT (user_id, exercise_id) DO UPDATE SET
    best_est_1rm_kg     = MAX(excluded.best_est_1rm_kg, COALESCE(exercise_records.best_est_1rm_kg, 0)),
    best_est_1rm_set_id = CASE WHEN excluded.best_est_1rm_kg > COALESCE(exercise_records.best_est_1rm_kg, 0)
                               THEN excluded.best_est_1rm_set_id ELSE exercise_records.best_est_1rm_set_id END,
    best_est_1rm_at     = CASE WHEN excluded.best_est_1rm_kg > COALESCE(exercise_records.best_est_1rm_kg, 0)
                               THEN excluded.best_est_1rm_at ELSE exercise_records.best_est_1rm_at END,
    updated_at = unixepoch();
MAX() is idempotent: applying it twice with the same input is a no-op.

LIFETIME TOTALS are deliberately NOT touched here. `exercise_records.session_count / total_sets / total_reps / total_volume_kg` are sums, and a sum is the one thing that cannot be made replay-safe by MAX or by recomputation-in-the-hot-path. They roll up ONCE, in `finishWorkoutSession`, gated on the status transition being the thing that does the work:
  UPDATE workout_logs SET status = 'finished', finished_at = unixepoch(),
         duration_seconds = unixepoch() - started_at
   WHERE id = :log AND user_id = :me AND status = 'active';
`changes = 0` → already finished → return `{ ok: true, alreadyFinished: true }` and skip every rollup. A replayed finish therefore adds nothing, exactly as a replayed set check does.

FINALLY, the queue flush. `syncOfflineQueue({ userId, ops })` runs the whole reconnect batch as ONE IMMEDIATE transaction — one worker call, one write-lock acquisition — applying the identical guards per op and returning a per-op `{ accepted | replayed }` array so the player can prune its queue precisely rather than clearing it on a blanket 200.
designs.ownership:
First, a correction the design depends on: THERE IS NO `role = 'client'`. `001_init.sql:18` is `CHECK (role IN ('user','coach','admin'))`. A "client" is a `users` row with role `'user'` that appears as `coach_clients.client_id`. Nothing below keys on a role for row access; roles gate ENDPOINTS (403), rows gate DATA (404).

EXECUTION TABLES — direct, no join:
- `workout_logs`, `workout_log_entries`, `workout_log_sets`, `exercise_records`, `workout_prs`, `workout_exercise_grants`, `calendar_feed_tokens`: the predicate is literally `AND user_id = ?` with `?` always `req.user.id`. This is why `user_id` is denormalised onto entries AND sets — the hottest write in the product proves ownership without a single join, and two BEFORE INSERT triggers (`trg_workout_log_entries_parent`, `trg_workout_log_sets_parent`) RAISE(ABORT) if the copy ever disagrees with its parent, so the denormalisation cannot be used to forge a claim.
- The guard is in the write: `UPDATE workout_log_sets SET ... WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ? AND ? > last_client_seq`. Never a preceding SELECT that decides.

AUTHORING TABLES — always through the plan:
- `workout_plans` write: `WHERE id = ? AND owner_id = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL`.
- `workout_plan_days` / `workout_plan_items` / `workout_plan_item_sets` have NO owner column and must never be addressed by their own id alone. The guard is a correlated EXISTS inside the UPDATE, which SQLite supports and which keeps the check and the write in one statement:
    UPDATE workout_plan_items SET position = ?
     WHERE id = ?
       AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM workout_plan_days d
                     JOIN workout_plans p ON p.id = d.plan_id
                    WHERE d.id = workout_plan_items.day_id
                      AND p.owner_id = ? AND p.deleted_at IS NULL);
  `changes = 0` → 404. An item belonging to another coach's plan is indistinguishable from an item that never existed.
- Client READ of an assigned plan: `WHERE p.client_id = ? AND p.deleted_at IS NULL AND p.status <> 'draft'` — a client cannot see a plan their coach has not published.

CROSS-USER READS (coach → client) — keyed on the LINK, never on the client's user id. This copies `onboarding/routes.js:255-265` verbatim, and the URL shape must be `/api/v1/clients/:linkId/plans`, not `/clients/:userId/...`:
    const link = await db.get(
      `SELECT client_id FROM coach_clients WHERE id = ? AND coach_id = ? AND status = 'active'`,
      [linkId, req.user.id]);
    if (!link) return sendError(res, 404, ERR.NOT_FOUND, 'not found');
Every subsequent query is then scoped with `link.client_id`, never with anything from the URL.

ARCHIVING ENDS ACCESS IMMEDIATELY, in four distinct ways:
1. `status = 'active'` is required by the link lookup above (the STRICTER of the two predicates live in the repo today — `coaching/routes.js:119` uses `<> 'archived'`, `onboarding/routes.js:261` uses `= 'active'`; for cross-user data reads the design takes `= 'active'` deliberately, so an 'invited' link that was never accepted also grants nothing). Archiving sets `status='archived'`, so the SELECT returns no row on the very next request — with the SAME access token. There is no stale grant to expire, because there is no claim in the JWT to be stale.
2. Coach WRITES to an assigned plan additionally require the live link, so an archived coach cannot edit a plan they own but no longer coach:
    UPDATE workout_plans SET title = ?
     WHERE id = ? AND owner_id = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL
       AND (client_id IS NULL
            OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM coach_clients cc
                        WHERE cc.client_id = workout_plans.client_id
                          AND cc.coach_id = ? AND cc.status = 'active'));
3. The archive endpoint gains one statement, in the SAME transaction as the status flip:
    DELETE FROM workout_exercise_grants WHERE user_id = ? AND granted_by = ?;
   The coach's private exercise library is re-hidden from the client the moment the link is archived. The client's HISTORY is untouched, because `workout_log_entries.exercise_name_snapshot` renders it without needing read access to the exercise row at all.
4. The client keeps everything they own. Archiving is the coach losing access, not the client losing their training log — `workout_logs` and every row beneath it are keyed on `user_id`, and the coach was only ever a reader.

MISS SEMANTICS: every ownership miss above returns 404, never 403 — a 403 confirms the id is real, which is enough to enumerate another coach's clients or another client's sessions (`exercises/routes.js:22-25`). 403 is reserved for endpoint-level role gates (`requireCoach`), which leak nothing about which rows exist.
weaknesses: THE `last_client_seq` GUARD HAS A SILENT DATA-LOSS MODE, and it is the worst thing in this design. The guard trusts the client's counter to be monotonic. A client that reinstalls, clears storage, or switches devices mid-session restarts its counter at 1, and every subsequent write is then dropped by `:seq > last_client_seq` — reported to the user as `replayed: true`, i.e. as SUCCESS. The client sees checkmarks that never persisted. Mitigations exist (define seq as milliseconds since `client_started_at`; have the server return the current `last_client_seq` on every response so the client can fast-forward; refuse a seq that regresses by more than a threshold and force a resync) but none of them are in the schema, and the failure is silent by default. If one thing in this design gets a dedicated regression test, it is this.

`prev_entry_id` IS FROZEN AT MATERIALISATION, SO BACKFILL BREAKS IT. A client who starts today's session at 06:00 and then logs yesterday's missed workout at 07:00 leaves today's prev pointers aimed at the session before last. The pointer is by design immutable, which means there is no repair path short of a recompute job — and I have not designed one. Anyone who logs sessions out of order (which is common: people catch up on Sunday) gets a quietly wrong 'previous' column. The window-function alternative I rejected does not have this bug.

ONE ACTIVE SESSION PER USER IS A UX CLIFF. `idx_workout_logs_one_active` is a hard partial UNIQUE index. A client who forgets to tap Finish yesterday cannot start today's workout at all — the INSERT throws SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE, which under the current error handling (`lib/http.js:62-63`, no typed error mapping) surfaces as a generic 500, not as a useful message. The route must catch it and offer 'resume or discard', and the stale-session sweeper (finish sessions with ≥1 completed set and no activity for 12h; abandon those with none) must actually be built. Neither is schema.

`exercise_records` IS A CACHE AND NOTHING DETECTS DRIFT. If any future write path forgets to maintain it, PR badges go quietly wrong and no constraint fires. `needs_recompute` handles the one case I anticipated (an edit lowering a record-holding set); it does nothing about a bug I did not anticipate. A periodic verification job comparing the cache against `MAX()` over history is the obvious answer and is not designed here.

THE BODY-AREA → MUSCLE-GROUP MAP IS CRUDE AND WILL ANNOY REAL USERS. 'Avoid knee' removes everything touching quads, hamstrings, calves and glutes — that is squats, lunges, leg press AND leg extension, when the client can usually do two of those fine. Worse, it MISSES exercises that load a joint without training its muscles: a plank stresses wrists, a bench press stresses shoulders. The honest fix is per-exercise joint tagging across 1652 rows, which is a dataset problem I have not solved and have instead papered over with a lookup table.

EPLEY IS BAKED INTO A GENERATED COLUMN, WHICH IS THE HARDEST PLACE TO CHANGE IT. Choosing one 1RM formula is a product decision, and I have put it somewhere that requires DROP COLUMN + ADD COLUMN plus dropping and recreating any index over it to revise — inside a migration system that cannot rebuild tables at all (no `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` inside a transaction). It is recoverable, but I traded flexibility for unforgeability and someone will curse me when they want Brzycki. The 12-rep cap also means high-rep athletes get no 1RM curve whatsoever, which for a bodyweight-focused client is most of their training.

CIRCUIT EXECUTION ORDER IS NOT RECORDED. `group_index` groups a superset, but sets are materialised per entry sequentially, so the real interleaving — A1, B1, A2, B2 — is lost. The player can render it from the grouping; the log cannot reconstruct what actually happened, and `rest_taken_seconds` inside a circuit becomes close to meaningless.

`client_uid` TRUSTS THE CLIENT NOT TO COLLIDE. A buggy player that reuses a uid silently merges two sessions, because `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` resolves to the existing row without complaint. There is no server-side detection, and the failure looks like data loss to the user.

13 NEW TABLES AND 6 NEW NAMED WORKER TRANSACTIONS LAND ON A CODEBASE WITH ZERO OF EITHER AND NO TEST SUITE (`backend/tests/` does not exist; the only coverage is `scripts/smoke.js`). The named-transaction mechanism is unexercised outside `migrate`. This design is a large step for a system whose regression net is one smoke script, and the idempotency claims above are claims until something replays a queue against a real database and checks the PR count.

designs.name: 009_workout_plans.sql — copy-on-assign authoring, materialised schedule, snapshot logs
designs.thesis: A template is a mould, never a live link: assigning deep-copies the plan, logging deep-copies the prescription, so a coach can edit anything at any time without silently rewriting what a client is doing tomorrow or what they did last month — and every ordering, PR and total in the schema is either guarded inside its own UPDATE or recomputed by aggregate, never incremented.

tables.name: workout_plans
tables.purpose: The plan DOCUMENT. One table for all four kinds of plan (coach template, client instance, self-coached personal plan, product-shipped system starter); `scope` discriminates and a table-level CHECK makes every incoherent owner combination unrepresentable. `source_plan_id` is provenance only — never a live link.
tables.ddl:
-- The plan document. `is_template` from the roadmap is COLLAPSED into `scope`: a separate
-- boolean would permit `is_template = 1 AND client_link_id IS NOT NULL`, a state with no meaning
-- that every read would then have to defend against. One enum, one CHECK, no reachable nonsense.
--
-- `source_plan_id` records where an instance came from so the UI can say "cloned from PPL 6-day".
-- It is provenance, NOT a live link: editing the template does not touch the clone. See
-- plan_assignments' trigger, which makes that law structural rather than a convention.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_plans (
  id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,

  -- template : a coach's reusable mould. NOT assignable — it must be cloned first.
  -- client   : an instance bound to exactly one coach_clients link. Assignable.
  -- personal : a self-coached user's own plan. Assignable, no coach.
  -- system   : product-shipped starter, owner-less, translatable, clone-only.
  scope          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'template'
                 CHECK (scope IN ('template', 'client', 'personal', 'system')),

  -- The AUTHOR, always. For scope='client' this is the COACH, not the client — which is what
  -- makes "the client may read their plan but never edit it" a one-column predicate.
  owner_user_id  INTEGER REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- The link, never the client's user id: the link carries the proof of entitlement and dies
  -- when the coach archives it.
  client_link_id INTEGER REFERENCES coach_clients(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  source_plan_id INTEGER REFERENCES workout_plans(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,

  name            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 120),
  -- Diacritics folded at write time by lib/normalize.js, exactly as exercises.normalized_name.
  -- Carries the index that makes a 200-template library searchable without an FTS5 shadow.
  normalized_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  description     TEXT CHECK (description IS NULL OR length(description) <= 2000),

  -- Deliberately the SAME vocabulary as onboarding_profiles, kebab spelling included, so the
  -- suggestion matcher is an equality join and not a translation table of two enums.
  goal       TEXT CHECK (goal IS NULL OR goal IN
             ('strength','muscle','fat-loss','endurance','mobility','health','sport')),
  experience TEXT CHECK (experience IS NULL OR experience IN
             ('none','beginner','intermediate','advanced')),

  weeks           INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (weeks BETWEEN 1 AND 52),
  session_minutes INTEGER CHECK (session_minutes IS NULL OR session_minutes BETWEEN 10 AND 240),

  -- Optimistic-concurrency counter for structural edits at plan level (add/remove/rename days).
  -- Deliberately allowed to over-count: a false 409 costs a refetch, a missed one costs data.
  rev             INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (rev >= 0),

  -- A client must not watch a half-built week appear one exercise at a time. NULL = draft,
  -- invisible to the client; set once the coach publishes.
  published_at    INTEGER,

  created_at      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  updated_at      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  archived_at     INTEGER,

  CHECK (
    (scope IN ('template','personal') AND owner_user_id IS NOT NULL AND client_link_id IS NULL)
    OR (scope = 'client'  AND owner_user_id IS NOT NULL AND client_link_id IS NOT NULL)
    OR (scope = 'system'  AND owner_user_id IS NULL     AND client_link_id IS NULL)
  )
);

-- The coach's library screen: my templates / my clients' plans, live ones first.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_plans_owner_idx
  ON workout_plans (owner_user_id, scope, archived_at);
-- The client's "my plan" read and the coach's client-detail tab.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_plans_client_idx
  ON workout_plans (client_link_id, archived_at) WHERE client_link_id IS NOT NULL;
-- "Which clients are on this template?" — the query that makes a bulk re-clone previewable.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_plans_source_idx
  ON workout_plans (source_plan_id) WHERE source_plan_id IS NOT NULL;
-- Starter-library browse, filtered by the onboarding answers.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_plans_system_idx
  ON workout_plans (scope, goal, experience) WHERE scope = 'system';
-- Prefix search over the template library. Cheaper and simpler than a second FTS5 shadow, and
-- brain-gen.mjs excludes any table matching %_fts% from the generated docs anyway.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_plans_sort_idx ON workout_plans (normalized_name, id);

-- 008-form trigger with the WHEN guard, so it cannot recurse through its own UPDATE and so an
-- explicit updated_at written by a migration or a backfill is not silently clobbered.
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_workout_plans_touch
AFTER UPDATE ON workout_plans FOR EACH ROW
WHEN NEW.updated_at = OLD.updated_at
BEGIN
  UPDATE workout_plans SET updated_at = unixepoch() WHERE id = NEW.id;
END;

tables.name: workout_plan_translations
tables.purpose: Localised name/description for scope='system' starter plans. Coach-authored plan names are the coach's own words and are never translated — the same rule onboarding_profiles.notes already follows.
tables.ddl:
-- Only system plans are ever translated. A coach's plan name is the coach's own words in the
-- coach's own language, and machine-translating "Bence hét 3 – deload" for the client would be
-- worse than showing the original — the same call 008 already made for onboarding notes.
--
-- Rowid table with a surrogate id and a UNIQUE on the natural key, matching exercise_translations
-- and taxonomy_translations. It needs no FTS5 today, but the shape stays uniform so that adding
-- one later is a migration and not a rebuild — which this migration runner cannot perform.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_plan_translations (
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  plan_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_plans(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  lang        TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES languages(code) ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  name        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 120),
  description TEXT CHECK (description IS NULL OR length(description) <= 2000),
  origin      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'manual' CHECK (origin IN ('manual','dataset','machine')),
  updated_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  UNIQUE (plan_id, lang)
);

-- The read path filters lang first, exactly like idx_taxonomy_tr_lookup.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_plan_translations_lang_idx
  ON workout_plan_translations (lang, plan_id);

-- A coach's private plan has no business carrying translations: it would be an admin surface
-- onto private content. The write path is admin-only, and this is the backstop.
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_plan_translation_system_only
BEFORE INSERT ON workout_plan_translations FOR EACH ROW
WHEN (SELECT scope FROM workout_plans WHERE id = NEW.plan_id) <> 'system'
BEGIN
  SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'only a system plan may carry translations');
END;

tables.name: workout_plan_days
tables.purpose: A session slot inside a plan, addressed by (week_index, day_index) so a multi-week block is first-class and 'copy week' has a target. Carries the `rev` counter that every drag-reorder is guarded against.
tables.ddl:
-- A day is addressed by its SLOT, (week_index, day_index), not by a free-floating position.
-- That is what makes "copy week 1 into week 2" a single named transaction with an obvious
-- target, and what lets a 4-week periodised block exist without a second table.
--
-- `weekday` is optional and separate: some plans are "Day 1 / Day 2 / Day 3", some are
-- "Monday / Wednesday / Friday". Forcing either onto the other loses information the coach typed.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_plan_days (
  id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  plan_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_plans(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  week_index INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (week_index >= 0),
  -- No upper bound in SQL on purpose. zod bounds it to 0..20 and produces the 400; the CHECK is
  -- a backstop, and a raised CHECK reaches the route as a generic 500 (worker.js has no typed
  -- error mapping). An upper bound here would also collide with the reorder parking range.
  day_index  INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (day_index >= 0),
  weekday    INTEGER CHECK (weekday IS NULL OR weekday BETWEEN 0 AND 6),  -- 0 = Monday

  name       TEXT CHECK (name IS NULL OR length(trim(name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 80),
  -- An explicit rest day, not an empty day. The calendar must render "Rest", and an empty slot
  -- is indistinguishable from a day the coach forgot to fill in.
  is_rest    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (is_rest IN (0, 1)),
  notes      TEXT CHECK (notes IS NULL OR length(notes) <= 2000),

  -- THE concurrency guard. Every structural mutation of this day (reorder, insert, delete,
  -- regroup) begins with `UPDATE ... SET rev = rev + 1 WHERE id = ? AND rev = ?`. A stale client
  -- matches nothing, gets zero changes, and the named transaction throws instead of scrambling
  -- the order. Two coaches dragging at once is detected, not silently merged.
  rev        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (rev >= 0),

  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())
);

-- One day per slot. Without this, "copy week" run twice produces two week-2s and the calendar
-- picks one at random.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_plan_days_slot_unique
  ON workout_plan_days (plan_id, week_index, day_index);

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_workout_plan_days_touch
AFTER UPDATE ON workout_plan_days FOR EACH ROW
WHEN NEW.updated_at = OLD.updated_at
BEGIN
  UPDATE workout_plan_days SET updated_at = unixepoch() WHERE id = NEW.id;
END;

tables.name: workout_plan_groups
tables.purpose: Superset and circuit grouping as a real entity with its own rounds and rest, not a tag string. Items reference it; the group is NOT a container in the ordering, which is what lets grouping survive a drag.
tables.ddl:
-- A superset is not a label, it has behaviour: a circuit has rounds and a rest between rounds,
-- a superset has a rest after the pair. A TEXT tag on the item cannot hold any of that, and a
-- JSON blob would be a relation in a JSON column.
--
-- Crucially the group is NOT a container in the ordering. Items keep ONE linear `position` per
-- day and the group is a property of the item. The invariant that makes grouping survive a drag
-- is CONTIGUITY: all items sharing a group_id must be adjacent in `position`, validated by the
-- reorder transaction before it writes. An interleaved superset is not a superset, it is a bug —
-- so it is rejected rather than stored.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_plan_groups (
  id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  day_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_plan_days(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- superset : back-to-back, one pass per set.
  -- circuit  : N rounds through the whole group, rest between rounds.
  kind   TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('superset', 'circuit')),
  label  TEXT CHECK (label IS NULL OR length(trim(label)) BETWEEN 1 AND 24),  -- "A", "B1"
  rounds INTEGER CHECK (rounds IS NULL OR rounds BETWEEN 1 AND 50),
  rest_between_seconds INTEGER CHECK (rest_between_seconds IS NULL OR rest_between_seconds BETWEEN 0 AND 3600),
  rest_after_seconds   INTEGER CHECK (rest_after_seconds   IS NULL OR rest_after_seconds   BETWEEN 0 AND 3600),
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  -- A circuit without a round count is not executable by the player.
  CHECK (kind <> 'circuit' OR rounds IS NOT NULL)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_plan_groups_day_idx ON workout_plan_groups (day_id);

tables.name: workout_plan_items
tables.purpose: The prescription: one exercise in one day. Contiguous integer `position` under a UNIQUE(day_id, position), sets/reps OR time OR distance made explicit by `prescription_kind` plus a cross-column CHECK, and a nullable group_id constrained by trigger to the item's own day.
tables.ddl:
-- ORDERING — the decision this table is built around.
--
-- `position` is a plain contiguous INTEGER, 0..n-1, and a drag rewrites every sibling. That is
-- the choice a Jira backlog cannot afford and this table can: a workout day is 3–15 exercises
-- because a human has to perform it. Rewriting 12 rows inside one IMMEDIATE transaction on a
-- local SQLite file is sub-millisecond, and contiguity buys things a sparse or fractional rank
-- cannot: copy-day is a plain INSERT..SELECT with no renumbering, the player and the ICS export
-- need no tie-break heuristic, and a broken order is DETECTABLE (max(position) = count(*) - 1).
-- LexoRank never breaks and therefore never tells you it is wrong.
--
-- Concurrency is handled by workout_plan_days.rev, not by the ordering column — a fractional
-- rank does not prevent two simultaneous drags from interleaving, it only stops anyone noticing.
--
-- The UNIQUE index below makes "two items in slot 3" impossible at the storage layer. A
-- permutation would collide mid-transaction, so the reorder transaction runs TWO passes:
--   pass 1: UPDATE ... SET position = position + 1000000 WHERE day_id = ?   (one statement)
--   pass 2: UPDATE ... SET position = ?, group_id = ? WHERE id = ? AND day_id = ?  (n statements)
-- Pass 1 is a bijection into a range disjoint from 0..n-1, so it is provably collision-free, and
-- the parked values stay >= 0 so the CHECK holds throughout.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_plan_items (
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  day_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_plan_days(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  exercise_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES exercises(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  group_id    INTEGER REFERENCES workout_plan_groups(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  position    INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (position >= 0),

  -- Which of the three prescription shapes this is, stated rather than inferred from which
  -- columns happen to be NULL. The CHECK below makes the incoherent combinations unstorable.
  prescription_kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'reps'
                    CHECK (prescription_kind IN ('reps', 'time', 'distance')),

  target_sets       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 3 CHECK (target_sets BETWEEN 1 AND 20),
  -- Coaches prescribe ranges ("8–12"). A single number is min = max.
  target_reps_min   INTEGER CHECK (target_reps_min IS NULL OR target_reps_min BETWEEN 1 AND 500),
  target_reps_max   INTEGER CHECK (target_reps_max IS NULL OR target_reps_max BETWEEN 1 AND 500),
  target_seconds    INTEGER CHECK (target_seconds IS NULL OR target_seconds BETWEEN 1 AND 14400),
  target_distance_m INTEGER CHECK (target_distance_m IS NULL OR target_distance_m BETWEEN 1 AND 500000),

  -- KILOGRAMS, always. `onboarding_profiles.units` is a display preference and must never reach
  -- a write path as a discriminator (008 states it: nothing may be converted twice).
  target_weight_kg  REAL CHECK (target_weight_kg IS NULL OR target_weight_kg BETWEEN 0 AND 1000),
  -- Percentage-based programming. The concrete kg is computed by the SERVER from
  -- exercise_records.max_e1rm at read time — never sent by the client, never stored as if it were.
  target_pct_1rm    REAL CHECK (target_pct_1rm IS NULL OR target_pct_1rm BETWEEN 1 AND 150),
  target_rpe        REAL CHECK (target_rpe IS NULL OR target_rpe BETWEEN 1 AND 10),  -- REAL: 7.5 is real
  rest_seconds      INTEGER CHECK (rest_seconds IS NULL OR rest_seconds BETWEEN 0 AND 3600),
  -- Eccentric-pause-concentric-pause, e.g. '3-1-1-0'. GLOB in the house style of 002/004.
  tempo             TEXT CHECK (tempo IS NULL OR tempo GLOB '[0-9X]-[0-9X]-[0-9X]-[0-9X]'),
  notes             TEXT CHECK (notes IS NULL OR length(notes) <= 1000),

  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),

  CHECK (target_reps_max IS NULL OR target_reps_min IS NULL OR target_reps_max >= target_reps_min),
  -- Absolute load and percentage load are two answers to one question.
  CHECK (target_weight_kg IS NULL OR target_pct_1rm IS NULL),
  CHECK (
    (prescription_kind = 'reps'     AND target_reps_min   IS NOT NULL) OR
    (prescription_kind = 'time'     AND target_seconds    IS NOT NULL) OR
    (prescription_kind = 'distance' AND target_distance_m IS NOT NULL)
  )
);

-- One item per slot: duplicate positions become impossible rather than unlikely.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_plan_items_slot_unique
  ON workout_plan_items (day_id, position);
-- The player renders a group as one card: fetch its members in performance order.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_plan_items_group_idx
  ON workout_plan_items (group_id, position) WHERE group_id IS NOT NULL;
-- Serves the EXISTS clause that grants a client read access to a coach's private exercise
-- because it was prescribed to them. Without it that clause is a scan on every player open.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_plan_items_exercise_idx ON workout_plan_items (exercise_id);

-- A group belongs to a day; an item that joined a group on another day would render as a
-- superset that spans two sessions. `IS NOT` is null-safe, so a dangling group_id aborts too.
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_plan_item_group_same_day_ins
BEFORE INSERT ON workout_plan_items FOR EACH ROW
WHEN NEW.group_id IS NOT NULL
 AND (SELECT day_id FROM workout_plan_groups WHERE id = NEW.group_id) IS NOT NEW.day_id
BEGIN
  SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'a plan item may only join a group on its own day');
END;

-- Scoped with UPDATE OF so the reorder passes do not pay for a subquery on every column write.
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_plan_item_group_same_day_upd
BEFORE UPDATE OF day_id, group_id ON workout_plan_items FOR EACH ROW
WHEN NEW.group_id IS NOT NULL
 AND (SELECT day_id FROM workout_plan_groups WHERE id = NEW.group_id) IS NOT NEW.day_id
BEGIN
  SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'a plan item may only join a group on its own day');
END;

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_workout_plan_items_touch
AFTER UPDATE ON workout_plan_items FOR EACH ROW
WHEN NEW.updated_at = OLD.updated_at
BEGIN
  UPDATE workout_plan_items SET updated_at = unixepoch() WHERE id = NEW.id;
END;

tables.name: workout_plan_item_sets
tables.purpose: Optional SPARSE per-set override for ramps, warmup sets, drop sets and AMRAP finishers. Zero rows means the item-level prescription applies to all `target_sets` sets — the common case costs nothing.
tables.ddl:
-- A sparse override, not a replacement. An item with no rows here means "target_sets identical
-- sets at the item-level targets" and stores nothing extra; an item with rows overrides them
-- per set_index. This is the difference between a toy and something a strength coach can use:
-- 'warmup 40kg x8, work 3x5 @ 100, backoff 1x8 @ 80' is one item and four rows.
--
-- It is also where drop sets and AMRAP live — those are properties of a SET, not of an exercise,
-- which is why workout_plan_groups.kind deliberately does not list them.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_plan_item_sets (
  id        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  item_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_plan_items(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  set_index INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (set_index >= 0),
  set_kind  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'work'
            CHECK (set_kind IN ('warmup','work','backoff','dropset','amrap','failure')),

  target_reps       INTEGER CHECK (target_reps IS NULL OR target_reps BETWEEN 0 AND 500),
  target_seconds    INTEGER CHECK (target_seconds IS NULL OR target_seconds BETWEEN 1 AND 14400),
  target_distance_m INTEGER CHECK (target_distance_m IS NULL OR target_distance_m BETWEEN 1 AND 500000),
  target_weight_kg  REAL CHECK (target_weight_kg IS NULL OR target_weight_kg BETWEEN 0 AND 1000),
  target_pct_1rm    REAL CHECK (target_pct_1rm IS NULL OR target_pct_1rm BETWEEN 1 AND 150),
  target_rpe        REAL CHECK (target_rpe IS NULL OR target_rpe BETWEEN 1 AND 10),
  rest_seconds      INTEGER CHECK (rest_seconds IS NULL OR rest_seconds BETWEEN 0 AND 3600),
  CHECK (target_weight_kg IS NULL OR target_pct_1rm IS NULL)
);

-- One override per slot; the read path is ordered by it.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_plan_item_sets_slot_unique
  ON workout_plan_item_sets (item_id, set_index);

tables.name: plan_assignments
tables.purpose: The scheduling binding: which client, from which civil date, for how many cycles. Two BEFORE triggers make the copy-on-assign law STRUCTURAL — a template can never be assigned, only cloned first.
tables.ddl:
-- Content and schedule are two different questions, so they are two different tables. A plan is
-- a document; an assignment is "this client, starting Monday, three cycles". Re-running a block
-- is a second assignment row, not a second copy of the plan.
--
-- DATES ARE CIVIL DATES, encoded YYYYMMDD as an INTEGER — not epoch seconds. "Monday's workout"
-- is a day in the client's own calendar and must not shift when they fly to Tokyo. The value is
-- still an INTEGER, still sorts and range-scans correctly, and is still not an ISO string. Real
-- instants (started_at, completed_at, created_at) remain epoch seconds everywhere.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plan_assignments (
  id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  plan_id        INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_plans(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- NULL only for a self-coached personal plan. The triggers below keep it in step with the plan.
  client_link_id INTEGER REFERENCES coach_clients(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- Denormalised so the client's own "what am I doing today" query never joins coach_clients,
  -- and so a personal plan (no link) uses the same index as a coached one.
  client_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  assigned_by    INTEGER REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,

  starts_on      INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (starts_on BETWEEN 19700101 AND 21001231),
  ends_on        INTEGER CHECK (ends_on IS NULL OR ends_on BETWEEN 19700101 AND 21001231),
  -- How many times the plan's week-block repeats. Bounds the plan_schedule materialisation.
  repeat_cycles  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (repeat_cycles BETWEEN 1 AND 52),
  -- IANA zone, so the server can decide which civil day "today" is and ICS can emit a TZID.
  timezone       TEXT CHECK (timezone IS NULL OR length(timezone) BETWEEN 3 AND 64),

  -- Opaque random token, never a row id: it is the stable UID of every VEVENT this assignment
  -- emits, and a guessable one would let a stranger correlate calendar entries.
  ics_uid        TEXT NOT NULL,
  -- Bumped on every schedule change; becomes the ICS SEQUENCE so subscribed calendars update.
  rev            INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (rev >= 0),

  status         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active','paused','ended')),
  created_at     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  updated_at     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  ended_at       INTEGER,
  CHECK (ends_on IS NULL OR ends_on >= starts_on)
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plan_assignments_ics_unique ON plan_assignments (ics_uid);
-- The client's schedule and the Home card.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plan_assignments_client_idx
  ON plan_assignments (client_id, status, starts_on);
-- The coach's client-detail tab: what is this client currently on?
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plan_assignments_link_idx ON plan_assignments (client_link_id, status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plan_assignments_plan_idx ON plan_assignments (plan_id);

-- THE COPY-ON-ASSIGN LAW, made structural.
--
-- Without this the whole templates-are-copies decision is a convention that one forgetful route
-- breaks, and the first coach who fixes a typo in a template silently rewrites what forty clients
-- are doing tomorrow morning. A template must be cloned; the clone is what gets assigned.
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_plan_assignment_scope_ins
BEFORE INSERT ON plan_assignments FOR EACH ROW
WHEN (SELECT scope FROM workout_plans WHERE id = NEW.plan_id) NOT IN ('client','personal')
BEGIN
  SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'only a client or personal plan may be assigned; clone the template first');
END;

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_plan_assignment_scope_upd
BEFORE UPDATE OF plan_id ON plan_assignments FOR EACH ROW
WHEN (SELECT scope FROM workout_plans WHERE id = NEW.plan_id) NOT IN ('client','personal')
BEGIN
  SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'only a client or personal plan may be assigned; clone the template first');
END;

-- An instance is bound to exactly one link, and the assignment must target that same link.
-- For a personal plan both sides are NULL and `IS NOT` yields false, so nothing aborts.
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_plan_assignment_link
BEFORE INSERT ON plan_assignments FOR EACH ROW
WHEN (SELECT client_link_id FROM workout_plans WHERE id = NEW.plan_id) IS NOT NEW.client_link_id
BEGIN
  SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'assignment must target the link its plan belongs to');
END;

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_plan_assignments_touch
AFTER UPDATE ON plan_assignments FOR EACH ROW
WHEN NEW.updated_at = OLD.updated_at
BEGIN
  UPDATE plan_assignments SET updated_at = unixepoch() WHERE id = NEW.id;
END;

tables.name: plan_schedule
tables.purpose: One materialised row per planned session: (assignment, cycle, plan day) → a civil date. Makes the calendar week view, the ICS feed, the Home 'today' card and adherence all indexed point/range lookups, and makes 'push Thursday to Friday' a single guarded UPDATE.
tables.ddl:
-- Materialised, not computed from a recurrence rule.
--
-- Coaches move individual sessions constantly ("push Thursday to Friday, she's travelling"). A
-- rule-based schedule turns that into an exception list, which is a second data model bolted onto
-- the first. One row per session makes the move a single guarded UPDATE, the calendar week a
-- range scan, the Home card a point lookup, and ICS a straight SELECT — one VEVENT per row.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plan_schedule (
  id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  assignment_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES plan_assignments(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  plan_day_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_plan_days(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- Denormalised from the assignment: the Home card must not join two tables to answer
  -- "what am I doing today", and this column carries the index that answers it.
  client_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

  scheduled_on  INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (scheduled_on BETWEEN 19700101 AND 21001231),
  -- The original date, kept when the session was moved, so the coach can see the drift and
  -- adherence can distinguish "late" from "never".
  moved_from_on INTEGER CHECK (moved_from_on IS NULL OR moved_from_on BETWEEN 19700101 AND 21001231),
  -- Which repetition of the plan's block this row belongs to (0-based).
  cycle_index   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (cycle_index >= 0),
  -- Soft flag in the house style, not a status enum: "done" has exactly one source of truth,
  -- the workout_logs row. Only "skipped" needs recording, because it leaves no log behind.
  skipped_at    INTEGER,
  created_at    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())
);

-- One occurrence per (assignment, cycle, day). A re-run of the materialisation after a crash
-- inserts nothing new rather than doubling every session.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plan_schedule_slot_unique
  ON plan_schedule (assignment_id, cycle_index, plan_day_id);
-- THE hot read: the Home "today" card, the calendar week range, the ICS feed window.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plan_schedule_today_idx ON plan_schedule (client_id, scheduled_on);
-- "Which scheduled sessions does this plan day feed?" — needed when the coach edits the plan.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plan_schedule_day_idx ON plan_schedule (plan_day_id);

-- The schedule's client must be the assignment's client, or a moved session could be handed to
-- the wrong person by a bug in one route.
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_plan_schedule_client_match
BEFORE INSERT ON plan_schedule FOR EACH ROW
WHEN (SELECT client_id FROM plan_assignments WHERE id = NEW.assignment_id) IS NOT NEW.client_id
BEGIN
  SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'plan_schedule.client_id must match its assignment');
END;

tables.name: workout_logs
tables.purpose: One performed session. Totals are stored but always RECOMPUTED by aggregate, never incremented, so a replayed write cannot inflate them. A partial unique index on schedule_id makes a double-tapped Start return the same log.
tables.ddl:
-- The session. `performed_on` is a civil date (YYYYMMDD) like the schedule; `started_at` and
-- `completed_at` are real instants in epoch seconds.
--
-- Every total here is DERIVED and is recomputed by aggregate over this log's sets on every write
-- that touches them. It is never incremented. That is the whole reason a replayed set-check
-- cannot inflate a client's volume: `SET total = (SELECT SUM(...))` is idempotent by
-- construction, `SET total = total + ?` is not.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_logs (
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  client_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

  -- Provenance, all soft. A workout that outlives its plan is still a workout, so nothing here
  -- cascades: deleting a plan must never delete a client's history.
  schedule_id INTEGER REFERENCES plan_schedule(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  plan_day_id INTEGER REFERENCES workout_plan_days(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  plan_id     INTEGER REFERENCES workout_plans(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,

  title       TEXT CHECK (title IS NULL OR length(trim(title)) BETWEEN 1 AND 120),
  performed_on INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (performed_on BETWEEN 19700101 AND 21001231),
  status      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'in_progress'
              CHECK (status IN ('in_progress', 'completed', 'abandoned')),

  started_at   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  completed_at INTEGER,
  duration_seconds INTEGER CHECK (duration_seconds IS NULL OR duration_seconds BETWEEN 0 AND 86400),

  total_volume_kg REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (total_volume_kg >= 0),
  total_sets      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (total_sets >= 0),
  total_reps      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (total_reps >= 0),

  -- Snapshot of the client's bodyweight at the time, so bodyweight-exercise volume and
  -- relative-strength graphs do not silently rewrite themselves when the profile changes.
  bodyweight_kg   REAL CHECK (bodyweight_kg IS NULL OR bodyweight_kg BETWEEN 25 AND 400),
  perceived_effort INTEGER CHECK (perceived_effort IS NULL OR perceived_effort BETWEEN 1 AND 10),
  notes TEXT CHECK (notes IS NULL OR length(notes) <= 2000),

  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  CHECK (status <> 'completed' OR completed_at IS NOT NULL)
);

-- A double-tapped "Start workout" is the client's most ordinary mistake. One live log per
-- scheduled session means the second tap finds the first log instead of creating a twin, and an
-- abandoned attempt does not block a genuine restart.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_logs_schedule_unique
  ON workout_logs (schedule_id) WHERE schedule_id IS NOT NULL AND status <> 'abandoned';
-- History list and the coach's client-progress tab.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_logs_client_idx
  ON workout_logs (client_id, performed_on DESC, id DESC);
-- "Resume your workout" — a tiny partial index over an almost always empty set.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_logs_open_idx
  ON workout_logs (client_id, status) WHERE status = 'in_progress';

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_workout_logs_touch
AFTER UPDATE ON workout_logs FOR EACH ROW
WHEN NEW.updated_at = OLD.updated_at
BEGIN
  UPDATE workout_logs SET updated_at = unixepoch() WHERE id = NEW.id;
END;

tables.name: workout_log_items
tables.purpose: One exercise inside a performed session, carrying a SNAPSHOT of the prescription and of the exercise's name. Its (client_id, exercise_id, performed_on DESC) index is the single index behind PREVIOUS-performance, the progress graph and PR recomputation.
tables.ddl:
-- The log is a SNAPSHOT, and that is the same decision as "a template is a mould", one level
-- down. The coach editing tomorrow's plan must not rewrite what the client did yesterday, and a
-- plan edit mid-session must not change the workout under the client's thumb. So every target
-- the player displays is copied here by the SERVER when the workout starts, and nothing on this
-- row depends on a plan item still existing or still saying the same thing.
--
-- `exercise_name_snapshot` exists for the same reason: an exercise may legitimately be renamed,
-- and a training log that retroactively renames what you did is wrong. It also keeps history
-- readable if the exercise row is ever hard-deleted (a coach's account deletion cascades into
-- their custom exercises).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_log_items (
  id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  log_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_logs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- Denormalised from the log. It exists solely to carry the history index below, which is the
  -- hottest read in the product: opening the player fires one per exercise.
  client_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

  exercise_id            INTEGER REFERENCES exercises(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  exercise_name_snapshot TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(exercise_name_snapshot)) BETWEEN 1 AND 200),
  plan_item_id           INTEGER REFERENCES workout_plan_items(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,

  -- Grouping snapshot: two plain scalars, not an FK and not a JSON blob. The group it came from
  -- may be regrouped or deleted tomorrow; how it was PERFORMED is fixed.
  group_ordinal INTEGER CHECK (group_ordinal IS NULL OR group_ordinal >= 0),
  group_kind    TEXT CHECK (group_kind IS NULL OR group_kind IN ('superset','circuit')),

  position INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (position >= 0),

  prescription_kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'reps'
                    CHECK (prescription_kind IN ('reps','time','distance')),
  target_sets       INTEGER CHECK (target_sets IS NULL OR target_sets BETWEEN 1 AND 20),
  target_reps_min   INTEGER,
  target_reps_max   INTEGER,
  target_seconds    INTEGER,
  target_distance_m INTEGER,
  target_weight_kg  REAL,   -- kg, already resolved from target_pct_1rm by the server
  target_rpe        REAL CHECK (target_rpe IS NULL OR target_rpe BETWEEN 1 AND 10),
  rest_seconds      INTEGER,

  -- Denormalised from the log so the history index is covering and needs no join.
  performed_on INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (performed_on BETWEEN 19700101 AND 21001231),
  notes TEXT CHECK (notes IS NULL OR length(notes) <= 1000),
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_log_items_slot_unique
  ON workout_log_items (log_id, position);
-- THE index. Serves three separate features off one B-tree: the player's PREVIOUS column
-- ("last time you did this: 4x8 @ 80"), the per-exercise progress graph, and the full
-- recomputation of an exercise_records row after a logged set is edited or deleted.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_log_items_history_idx
  ON workout_log_items (client_id, exercise_id, performed_on DESC, id DESC);
-- Serves the "an exercise you have personally performed stays readable forever" clause of the
-- client-side exercise visibility predicate.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_log_items_exercise_idx ON workout_log_items (exercise_id);

-- The denormalised client_id must never drift from its log, or one bug hands a client another
-- client's history through the index above.
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_log_item_client_match
BEFORE INSERT ON workout_log_items FOR EACH ROW
WHEN (SELECT client_id FROM workout_logs WHERE id = NEW.log_id) IS NOT NEW.client_id
BEGIN
  SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'workout_log_items.client_id must match its log');
END;

tables.name: workout_log_sets
tables.purpose: The set row the player checks off. UNIQUE(log_item_id, set_index) is the natural key that makes 'set checked' an UPSERT rather than an append — which is the entire idempotency story, for the PR today and for the coin ledger later.
tables.ddl:
-- THE IDEMPOTENCY ANCHOR.
--
-- "Set checked" is not an event to append, it is an assertion about the state of set N of
-- exercise M in workout W. Modelled that way, the natural key IS the idempotency key: a replayed
-- check rewrites the same row with the same values instead of creating a second one. No
-- idempotency_keys table, no TTL sweeper, no stored response bodies.
--
-- Everything downstream inherits it: the PR upsert compares against the record and cannot fire
-- twice (see exercise_records), the log totals are recomputed by aggregate and cannot inflate,
-- and a future coin ledger keyed UNIQUE(source_type='workout_set', source_id) cannot double-award
-- because `id` here is stable across replays.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workout_log_sets (
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  log_item_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_log_items(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- Denormalised so the total-recompute aggregate is one indexed scan per log, not a join.
  log_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workout_logs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  set_index   INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (set_index >= 0),
  set_kind    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'work'
              CHECK (set_kind IN ('warmup','work','backoff','dropset','amrap','failure')),

  -- What was PRESCRIBED for this set, snapshotted at start. The player's grey placeholder.
  target_reps      INTEGER CHECK (target_reps IS NULL OR target_reps BETWEEN 0 AND 500),
  target_seconds   INTEGER,
  target_distance_m INTEGER,
  target_weight_kg REAL,
  target_rpe       REAL CHECK (target_rpe IS NULL OR target_rpe BETWEEN 1 AND 10),

  -- What was actually PERFORMED. NULL until the set is checked. Kilograms, always.
  weight_kg  REAL    CHECK (weight_kg IS NULL OR weight_kg BETWEEN 0 AND 1000),
  reps       INTEGER CHECK (reps IS NULL OR reps BETWEEN 0 AND 500),
  seconds    INTEGER CHECK (seconds IS NULL OR seconds BETWEEN 0 AND 14400),
  distance_m INTEGER CHECK (distance_m IS NULL OR distance_m BETWEEN 0 AND 500000),
  rpe        REAL    CHECK (rpe IS NULL OR rpe BETWEEN 1 AND 10),
  rest_taken_seconds INTEGER CHECK (rest_taken_seconds IS NULL OR rest_taken_seconds BETWEEN 0 AND 7200),

  completed_at INTEGER,
  -- The gold-frame badge. Written ONLY by recordSet, and only when the guarded record upsert
  -- actually moved a record — so it is set exactly once and a replay neither grants nor clears it.
  -- WHICH record it was is answered by exercise_records.source_set_id, not by a list column here:
  -- a comma-joined list of metrics would be a relation hiding in a TEXT column.
  is_pr INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (is_pr IN (0, 1)),

  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),

  -- A checked set that recorded nothing is a UI bug reaching storage.
  CHECK (completed_at IS NULL OR reps IS NOT NULL OR seconds IS NOT NULL OR distance_m IS NOT NULL)
);

-- The natural key, and the ON CONFLICT target of the whole set-check path.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_log_sets_slot_unique
  ON workout_log_sets (log_item_id, set_index);
-- The total recompute: SUM(weight_kg * reps) over one log's completed sets.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS workout_log_sets_log_idx ON workout_log_sets (log_id, completed_at);

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_workout_log_sets_touch
AFTER UPDATE ON workout_log_sets FOR EACH ROW
WHEN NEW.updated_at = OLD.updated_at
BEGIN
  UPDATE workout_log_sets SET updated_at = unixepoch() WHERE id = NEW.id;
END;

tables.name: exercise_records
tables.purpose: The best-ever value per (user, exercise, metric). A PR is detected by a guarded ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE excluded.value > value — the comparison lives INSIDE the UPDATE, so a replay reports zero changes and awards nothing.
tables.ddl:
-- PRs are DERIVED STATE, not an event stream, and that is what makes them replay-proof.
--
-- The set-check transaction upserts here with the comparison INSIDE the UPDATE:
--
--   INSERT INTO exercise_records (...) VALUES (...)
--   ON CONFLICT (user_id, exercise_id, metric) DO UPDATE SET
--     previous_value = exercise_records.value, value = excluded.value, ...
--   WHERE excluded.value > exercise_records.value;
--
-- changes === 1 means, and can only mean, a genuinely new best. A replayed set produces
-- excluded.value = exercise_records.value, the WHERE is false, changes === 0, no badge, no
-- future coin. There is no preceding SELECT to race against.
--
-- The 1RM FORMULA IS NOT IN THE SCHEMA. Epley lives in one JS module and its output is stored
-- here as a plain REAL under metric='max_e1rm'. A STORED generated column would have been
-- indexable and wrong: changing the formula would need a table rebuild, and the 12-step rebuild
-- is unavailable inside this migration runner (no BEGIN/COMMIT, no PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF).
-- With the value stored, a formula change is a recompute job.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS exercise_records (
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  exercise_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES exercises(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- snake_case bounded codes. max_weight: heaviest load moved. max_e1rm: the real strength PR.
  -- max_volume_set: weight x reps in one set. The rest cover bodyweight, holds and cardio.
  metric      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (metric IN
              ('max_weight','max_reps','max_e1rm','max_volume_set','max_duration','max_distance')),

  value       REAL NOT NULL CHECK (value > 0),
  -- The context that makes the number readable: "102.5 kg e1RM (85 kg x 6)".
  reps        INTEGER CHECK (reps IS NULL OR reps BETWEEN 0 AND 500),
  weight_kg   REAL CHECK (weight_kg IS NULL OR weight_kg BETWEEN 0 AND 1000),
  -- Which set holds the record. SET NULL rather than CASCADE: losing the pointer must not lose
  -- the record. It is also the flag that tells recomputeExerciseRecord it has work to do when a
  -- logged set is edited or deleted.
  source_set_id INTEGER REFERENCES workout_log_sets(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,

  achieved_on INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (achieved_on BETWEEN 19700101 AND 21001231),
  achieved_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  -- So the badge can say "+2.5 kg" instead of just "PR". Costs one column, earns the whole
  -- feeling of the moment.
  previous_value REAL CHECK (previous_value IS NULL OR previous_value >= 0),
  updated_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())
);

-- The ON CONFLICT target. Without it the guarded upsert is not expressible at all.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS exercise_records_unique
  ON exercise_records (user_id, exercise_id, metric);
-- "Recent PRs" on the client's profile and the coach's dashboard alerts.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS exercise_records_user_idx ON exercise_records (user_id, achieved_at DESC);
-- The player asks "which records does this set hold?" to label the badge, and
-- recomputeExerciseRecord asks "which records did the set I just edited hold?".
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS exercise_records_source_idx
  ON exercise_records (source_set_id) WHERE source_set_id IS NOT NULL;

tables.name: body_area_muscle_map
tables.purpose: The missing bridge between onboarding_limitations.body_area (13 joint-centric codes) and muscle_groups. Without it, 'avoid knee' cannot filter a single exercise — the two vocabularies do not meet anywhere in the current schema.
tables.ddl:
-- 008 chose a JOINT-centric vocabulary for limitations, correctly: people injure knees and
-- shoulders, which are not muscle groups. But exercises map to MUSCLE groups, so today
-- "avoid knee" cannot exclude a single exercise — the two vocabularies do not touch anywhere in
-- the schema. This is that missing edge, and it is what unblocks T2.5.4.
--
-- A junction with one small enum payload and no scalars: WITHOUT ROWID, exactly like
-- exercise_muscle_map. Admin-editable rather than a CHECK, because the mapping is a clinical
-- judgement that will be corrected without a migration.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS body_area_muscle_map (
  body_area TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (body_area IN (
    'neck','shoulder','elbow','wrist','upper-back','lower-back',
    'hip','knee','ankle','foot','chest','abdomen','other'
  )),
  muscle_group_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES muscle_groups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- 'primary' = severity 'avoid' excludes the exercise outright.
  -- 'secondary' = only 'avoid' on a primary excludes; secondary merely flags.
  role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'primary' CHECK (role IN ('primary', 'secondary')),
  PRIMARY KEY (body_area, muscle_group_id)
) WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS body_area_muscle_by_muscle ON body_area_muscle_map (muscle_group_id);

-- Seeded through the SLUG, never a literal id: muscle_groups ids are assigned by insertion order
-- and differ between a fresh database and an upgraded one.
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO body_area_muscle_map (body_area, muscle_group_id, role)
SELECT v.area, g.id, v.role
  FROM muscle_groups g
  JOIN (
    SELECT 'knee' AS area, 'quads' AS slug, 'primary' AS role
    UNION ALL SELECT 'knee','hamstrings','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'knee','glutes','secondary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'knee','calves','secondary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'hip','glutes','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'hip','hamstrings','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'hip','adductors','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'hip','abductors','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'hip','quads','secondary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'lower-back','lower-back','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'lower-back','glutes','secondary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'lower-back','hamstrings','secondary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'upper-back','lats','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'upper-back','traps','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'upper-back','rear-delts','secondary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'neck','neck','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'neck','traps','secondary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'shoulder','front-delts','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'shoulder','side-delts','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'shoulder','rear-delts','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'shoulder','chest','secondary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'elbow','biceps','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'elbow','triceps','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'elbow','forearms','secondary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'wrist','forearms','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'wrist','biceps','secondary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'wrist','triceps','secondary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'chest','chest','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'chest','front-delts','secondary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'abdomen','abs','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'abdomen','obliques','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'ankle','calves','primary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'ankle','quads','secondary'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'foot','calves','primary'
  ) v ON v.slug = g.slug;
-- 'other' maps to nothing on purpose: a free-text limitation the coach must read, not a filter.

tables.name: client_exercise_prefs
tables.purpose: The coach's explicit override of the suggestion heuristic, per client link: exclude this exercise, prefer that one, substitute a third. The escape hatch that makes an approximate body-area heuristic acceptable to ship.
tables.ddl:
-- The body_area heuristic is approximate by construction ("avoid knee" excluding every quad
-- movement is too blunt for a hip thrust). This is the coach's override, and it is why shipping
-- the heuristic is honest rather than reckless: when the machine is wrong, the coach corrects it
-- once and it stays corrected.
--
-- Keyed on the LINK, not the client's user id, so it dies with the coaching relationship and
-- never leaks one coach's judgement into another coach's suggestions for the same person.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS client_exercise_prefs (
  id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  client_link_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES coach_clients(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  exercise_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES exercises(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  preference     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (preference IN ('preferred', 'excluded')),
  -- "Use this instead" — what turns an exclusion from a hole in the plan into a swap.
  substitute_exercise_id INTEGER REFERENCES exercises(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  note       TEXT CHECK (note IS NULL OR length(note) <= 500),
  created_by INTEGER REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch()),
  CHECK (substitute_exercise_id IS NULL OR substitute_exercise_id <> exercise_id)
);

-- One verdict per exercise per client; two contradicting rows would make the filter
-- non-deterministic. Rowid table with a UNIQUE index rather than WITHOUT ROWID, following the
-- uniformity 004 argued for and 008 copied into onboarding_limitations.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS client_exercise_prefs_unique
  ON client_exercise_prefs (client_link_id, exercise_id);

tables.name: (ALTERs on existing tables)
tables.purpose: Two nullable columns the calendar and ICS export need: a per-link calendar feed token, and the client's IANA timezone. Both nullable because ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN in SQLite forbids a non-constant DEFAULT — `DEFAULT (unixepoch())` would fail at migration time.
tables.ddl:
-- The ICS feed URL must carry a secret, not a row id. Per LINK rather than per user, so a client
-- coached by two coaches gets two feeds, and so revoking a coach's relationship revokes their
-- calendar feed with it — the same "archiving ends access immediately" property the link already
-- gives every other read.
--
-- Nullable, generated lazily on the first ICS request: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN cannot carry a
-- non-constant DEFAULT, so `DEFAULT (hex(randomblob(16)))` would fail at migration time. This is
-- the same constraint that forced 006 to add must_change_credentials as a literal-default column.
ALTER TABLE coach_clients ADD COLUMN ics_token TEXT;

-- ADD COLUMN cannot carry UNIQUE either — but a partial unique INDEX can be created afterwards,
-- and it is strictly better here: it costs nothing for the rows that never request a feed.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS coach_clients_ics_token_unique
  ON coach_clients (ics_token) WHERE ics_token IS NOT NULL;

-- Which civil day is "today" for this client, and the TZID the ICS export must emit. IANA name.
-- It belongs with the rest of the profile the plan builder already reads.
ALTER TABLE onboarding_profiles ADD COLUMN timezone TEXT
  CHECK (timezone IS NULL OR length(timezone) BETWEEN 3 AND 64);

keyDecisions.decision: A coach editing a template does NOT change plans already assigned to clients. Assignment is a deep copy (clone-to-client), and `plan_assignments`' BEFORE INSERT trigger physically refuses any plan whose scope is not 'client' or 'personal'.
keyDecisions.rationale: Three separate arguments converge. (1) Safety: a coach must be able to fix a typo in a template at 23:00 without silently rewriting what forty clients do at 06:00. (2) Personalisation: a live link makes per-client edits impossible without a sparse-overlay diff layer, turning every plan read — including the guided player's, on a phone, on a train — into a three-way merge. (3) History: workout_log rows reference the prescription. If the template mutates, a completed log's 'prescribed 4x8 @ 80kg' retroactively becomes '5x5 @ 100kg'. A training log that rewrites itself is not a log. `source_plan_id` keeps the provenance so the UI can say 'cloned from PPL 6-day' and offer an explicit, previewable re-clone.
keyDecisions.rejected: A live FK from the instance to the template plus a `plan_item_overrides` sparse-overlay table. Rejected because it makes the hottest read path a merge, it cannot express 'delete this exercise for this client' without a tombstone row, and it corrupts history. Also rejected: a `scope='team'` plan read live by every member — it looks like the answer to 'I want one edit to reach everyone', but it strands a client's logs the moment they leave the team, and it creates a second ownership predicate. Team assignment is instead a fan-out of N clones.

keyDecisions.decision: `position` is a plain contiguous INTEGER, 0..n-1, under a UNIQUE(day_id, position), and a drag rewrites every sibling row in the day.
keyDecisions.rationale: The O(n) rewrite that disqualifies contiguous positions in a 10 000-row backlog is 12 UPDATEs here, because a workout day is 3–15 exercises — a human has to perform it. Sub-millisecond inside one IMMEDIATE transaction on a local file. Contiguity then buys three things a sparse or fractional order cannot: copy-day is a plain INSERT..SELECT with no renumber pass, the calendar/player/ICS need no tie-break heuristic, and a corrupted order is DETECTABLE (max(position) must equal count(*)-1). LexoRank never breaks and therefore never tells you it is wrong.
keyDecisions.rejected: Sparse gaps (100/200/300) — a single-row write, but exhausts unpredictably and the renumber pass is the O(n) rewrite again, arriving at the worst possible moment. LexoRank/fractional TEXT ranks — never exhausts, but it is real machinery for a 15-row list, and critically it does NOT solve concurrent drags, it only makes them silent. Linked list (prev_id/next_id) — reading a day in order needs a recursive CTE and one broken link is unrecoverable.

keyDecisions.decision: Concurrency safety for reordering is `workout_plan_days.rev`, not the ordering column. Every structural mutation of a day begins with `UPDATE workout_plan_days SET rev = rev + 1 WHERE id = ? AND plan_id = ? AND rev = ?`; zero changes means the client's view was stale and the transaction throws (route maps it to 409 with the current rev, UI refetches and replays the drag).
keyDecisions.rationale: What a coach actually needs when two devices reorder the same day is DETECTION, not lock-freedom. Silently merging two drags produces an order nobody intended and nobody is told about. The guard is inside the UPDATE — no preceding SELECT, no race — which is the same shape as the proven `UPDATE invite_codes SET uses = uses + 1 WHERE uses < max_uses` in coaching/routes.js:268.
keyDecisions.rejected: An `updated_at` timestamp comparison (second-granularity epoch seconds collide on fast successive edits). Row-level locking (SQLite has one writer, not row locks). Last-writer-wins with no counter — cheap, and the reason drag-reorder bugs are unreproducible in every product that ships it.

keyDecisions.decision: The reorder is a NAMED worker transaction `savePlanDayOrder`, and it runs the position updates in TWO passes. Pass 1: `UPDATE workout_plan_items SET position = position + 1000000 WHERE day_id = ?` (one statement). Pass 2: `UPDATE workout_plan_items SET position = ?, group_id = ? WHERE id = ? AND day_id = ?`, n times.
keyDecisions.rationale: The UNIQUE(day_id, position) index makes 'two items in slot 3' impossible at the storage layer — but any permutation collides mid-transaction, and SQLite has no DEFERRABLE unique. Pass 1 is a bijection into a range disjoint from 0..n-1, so it is provably collision-free, and the parked values stay >= 0 so the CHECK holds throughout. It must be a NAMED transaction rather than `writeTx` because writeTx cannot inspect the rev-guard result and cannot branch — worker.js:97-99 says so explicitly, and the join-code comment warns the guard-in-UPDATE pattern does not generalise to 'step 2 must not happen when step 1 fails'. Both halves are required: `export function savePlanDayOrder({...})` in src/db/worker.js doing getDb().transaction(...).immediate(...), and `export const savePlanDayOrder = (args) => pool.run(args, { name: 'savePlanDayOrder' });` in src/db/index.js.
keyDecisions.rejected: Dropping the UNIQUE index and trusting the transaction to be correct — cheaper, but it turns a class of ordering bug from 'impossible' into 'silent'. A single-pass ordering of the UPDATEs to dodge collisions — impossible in general for an arbitrary permutation.

keyDecisions.decision: Reorder sends ITEM IDS ONLY (`[{item_id, position, group_id}]`) and updates in place. It is NOT the delete-then-insert replace-in-place that onboarding/routes.js:189 uses for the equipment set.
keyDecisions.rationale: An onboarding equipment set has no per-row identity worth preserving — it is a set of ids. A plan item is an entity: it carries the coach's cue text, it is referenced by workout_log_items.plan_item_id, and the coach's undo stack points at it. Churning its id to move it one slot up is destructive. The named transaction validates BEFORE any write that the payload length equals the day's item count and that every id belongs to the day — a partial payload would otherwise leave rows parked at +1000000.
keyDecisions.rejected: Replace-in-place (delete all, re-insert) — it matches the existing precedent and yields contiguity for free, but it invalidates every id in the day on every drag. Separately rejected: a delta/patch API ('move item 3 to index 7') — smaller payload, but the server then has to reconstruct the client's intended final state, and any disagreement about the starting state produces a wrong order with no way to notice.

keyDecisions.decision: Superset/circuit grouping is a real table (`workout_plan_groups`) referenced by a nullable `group_id`, but the group is NOT a container in the ordering. Items keep ONE linear `position` per day, and the invariant is CONTIGUITY: all items sharing a group_id must be adjacent, validated before the reorder writes.
keyDecisions.rationale: A superset IS 'do these back to back'. An interleaved superset is not a superset, it is a bug, so it is rejected rather than stored. A single linear sequence means the player walks one list, ICS emits one ordered body, and 'drag an item out of a group' has an obvious meaning (clear group_id) rather than requiring a nested reorder protocol. A real table rather than a tag string because a circuit has rounds and a rest-between-rounds, and a superset has a rest-after — behaviour a TEXT tag cannot hold and a JSON blob must not.
keyDecisions.rejected: `superset_group TEXT` tag on the item — no place for rounds or rest, and nothing prevents an interleave. Two-level ordering (groups ordered among top-level entries, items ordered within groups) — the correct normalisation, rejected because reading a day then needs a UNION of grouped and ungrouped entries ordered together, and every drag has to decide which of two sequences it is editing.

keyDecisions.decision: Templates, client instances, personal plans and system starters are ONE table discriminated by `scope`. The roadmap's `is_template` boolean is collapsed into that enum.
keyDecisions.rationale: A separate boolean permits `is_template = 1 AND client_link_id IS NOT NULL` — a state with no meaning that every read would then have to defend against. One enum plus one table-level CHECK makes every incoherent owner combination physically unrepresentable, which is strictly stronger than any route-level convention.
keyDecisions.rejected: Separate `workout_templates` and `workout_plans` tables — clean-looking, but clone-to-client then needs two nearly identical copy transactions, `source_plan_id` cannot be a self-FK, and every 'show me all plans' query becomes a UNION. Also rejected: `is_template INTEGER` alongside `scope`, i.e. two sources of one truth.

keyDecisions.decision: Civil dates (`starts_on`, `scheduled_on`, `performed_on`, `achieved_on`) are stored as YYYYMMDD INTEGERs, not epoch seconds. Real instants (`started_at`, `completed_at`, all `*_at`) stay epoch seconds.
keyDecisions.rationale: A civil date is not a timestamp. 'Monday's workout' is a day in the client's own calendar, and an epoch instant for it shifts when they fly to Tokyo or when DST moves — silently reassigning their leg day. YYYYMMDD is still an INTEGER (the type rule holds), still sorts and range-scans correctly for the calendar week and the ICS window, and is timezone-independent by construction. The client's IANA zone lives on onboarding_profiles.timezone so the server can decide which civil day 'today' is.
keyDecisions.rejected: Epoch seconds at local midnight — the standard choice, rejected because 'local' is a property of the reader, not of the row, and a stored local-midnight instant is wrong for every other reader including the coach. Also rejected: a TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD' — readable, but the repo has no ISO strings anywhere and it costs a collation on every range scan.

keyDecisions.decision: Every derived counter in this schema is RECOMPUTED BY AGGREGATE, never incremented. `workout_logs.total_volume_kg / total_sets / total_reps` are set from `SELECT SUM(...)` over the log's sets. The only incremented columns are the `rev` counters, which are deliberately allowed to over-count.
keyDecisions.rationale: This is the general law behind the idempotency requirement. `SET total = (SELECT SUM(...))` is idempotent by construction; `SET total = total + ?` is not, and a retried set-check would inflate a client's volume forever with no way to detect it after the fact. The aggregate is bounded — one log is ~40 set rows behind `workout_log_sets_log_idx` — so correctness costs nothing measurable. A false 409 from an over-counted `rev` costs a refetch; a missed one costs data.
keyDecisions.rejected: Incrementing the totals in the set-check transaction (one fewer scan, permanently wrong under any retry). Storing no totals at all and aggregating on read (correct, but the coach dashboard's adherence and weekly-volume queries would then aggregate across every client's every set on every page load).

keyDecisions.decision: The log is a SNAPSHOT of the prescription and of the exercise's name; it does not depend on plan-item identity. `workout_log_items` copies every target at start, keeps `exercise_name_snapshot TEXT NOT NULL`, and its `plan_item_id` / `exercise_id` are both nullable with ON DELETE SET NULL.
keyDecisions.rationale: Same decision as 'a template is a mould', one level down. A plan edit mid-session must not change the workout under the client's thumb, and an exercise rename ('Barbell Bench Press' → 'Bench Press (Barbell)') must not retroactively rename what they did. It also survives the real hard-delete path: `exercises.owner_id REFERENCES users ON DELETE CASCADE` means deleting a coach's account destroys their custom exercises, and without the snapshot every client's history of those exercises would go blank.
keyDecisions.rejected: A hard FK from log sets to plan items (any reorder or edit dangles or cascades into history). Resolving targets by joining the plan at read time (cheapest storage, but the displayed history changes whenever the coach edits the plan — the exact failure this whole design is built to avoid).

keyDecisions.decision: A coach's `private` exercise becomes readable to a client through a SECOND visibility predicate used only on plan/player/history reads — never on library browse. It adds two EXISTS clauses to the existing `VISIBLE`: prescribed-to-me-through-an-active-link, and personally-performed-by-me.
keyDecisions.rationale: exercises/routes.js:26's `VISIBLE` makes a coach's private exercise invisible to their own client, so a plan built from the coach's custom library would 404 for the client — the schema is silent on this today and the design must not be. Access follows the PRESCRIPTION (revoked the instant the link is archived, because the EXISTS joins coach_clients on status='active') rather than the relationship, so it never leaks the coach's whole library. The performed-by-me clause is the durability half: an exercise you have actually done stays readable forever, even after the plan that prescribed it is deleted. Both EXISTS are index-backed (`workout_plan_items_exercise_idx`, `workout_log_items_exercise_idx`).
keyDecisions.rejected: Extending the single global `VISIBLE` with `OR EXISTS (coach_clients ...
